    reference_title: Epidemiology of Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy and of Intellectual Disability and Epilepsy in Children.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Point prevalence for the broad group of children with epilepsy and
      developmental impairment was 175/100,000 children (95% CI 149-203; DEE 112
      and ID+E 63/100,000 children).
    explanation: >-
      Reports DEE point prevalence of 112 per 100,000 children. The study measures
      DEE of all etiologies rather than the genetic subgroup alone, so it bounds
      this entry's occurrence from above rather than measuring it.
- population: Wellington region, New Zealand (population-based paediatric cohort)
  measure_type: LIFETIME_PREVALENCE
  prevalence_class: ABOVE_1_IN_1000
  rate_per_100000: 169.0
  rate_low: 144.0
  rate_high: 199.0
  notes: >-
    Cumulative incidence of DEE per 100,000 children (approximately 1 in 590),
    accrued to age 16 years, for DEE overall rather than the genetic subgroup
    specifically. Recorded as LIFETIME_PREVALENCE rather than ANNUAL_INCIDENCE:
    the source reports a cumulative proportion affected by age 16, not a rate of
    new cases per year, and reading it as an annual rate would overstate DEE
    occurrence by roughly an order of magnitude.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:36581463
    reference_title: Epidemiology of Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy and of Intellectual Disability and Epilepsy in Children.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Cumulative incidence for DEE was 169/100,000 children (95% CI
      144-199)
    explanation: >-
      Reports cumulative incidence of DEE. The measure covers DEE of all
      etiologies rather than genetic DEE alone, so it bounds this entry's
      occurrence from above rather than measuring it.
inheritance:
- name: Autosomal dominant inheritance
  inheritance_term:
    preferred_term: Autosomal dominant inheritance
    term:
      id: HP:0000006
      label: Autosomal dominant inheritance
  description: >-
    Genetic DEE is most commonly regarded as a de novo dominant disease class,
    and the highest-prevalence individual entities (SCN1A, SCN2A, STXBP1,
    KCNQ2, SCN8A) are indeed de novo autosomal dominant, so affected children
    typically have unaffected parents. Parental germline mosaicism gives a small
    but non-zero sibling recurrence risk. Note that this reflects the
    distribution of *cases*: counted by *gene*, more DEE genes follow autosomal
    recessive than dominant inheritance.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39237642
    reference_title: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Genetic DEEs are most commonly regarded as de novo  dominant disorders ;
      however, more DEE genes follow autosomal recessive than dominant
      inheritance, with a small number
      following X-linked or mitochondrial inheritance patterns
    explanation: >-
      Establishes de novo dominant inheritance as the prevailing mode while
      making explicit the gene-count versus case-count distinction that this
      description records.
  - reference: PMID:39613335
    reference_title: National survey on the prevalence of single-gene aetiologies for genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathies in Italy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in genes with an autosomal
      dominant inheritance pattern occurred in 77% (n=1207) patients; 17%
      (n=271) in X-linked genes and 6% (n=90) in genes with autosomal recessive
      inheritance.
    explanation: >-
      Quantifies the case-level distribution of inheritance modes across 1568
      molecularly diagnosed genetic DEE patients, confirming autosomal dominant
      as the predominant mode by case count.
  - reference: PMID:39237642
    reference_title: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Parental mosaicism places parents at an
      increased risk of having a second child with a DEE, as a small population
      of their sperm or ova carry the
      pathogenic variant.
    explanation: >-
      Supports the non-zero sibling recurrence risk stated in this description,
      which would otherwise be an uncited claim.
- name: Autosomal recessive inheritance
  inheritance_term:
    preferred_term: Autosomal recessive inheritance
    term:
      id: HP:0000007
      label: Autosomal recessive inheritance
  description: >-
    Counted by gene rather than by case, more DEE genes follow autosomal
    recessive than dominant inheritance. Biallelic forms are individually rarer
    but collectively numerous, and are enriched in consanguineous families and
    among metabolic and glycosylation-pathway DEE genes.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39237642
    reference_title: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      more DEE genes follow autosomal recessive than dominant inheritance
    explanation: >-
      Directly supports autosomal recessive inheritance as the most common mode
      when DEE genes are counted individually.
  - reference: PMID:39613335
    reference_title: National survey on the prevalence of single-gene aetiologies for genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathies in Italy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      6%
      (n=90) in genes with autosomal recessive inheritance.
    explanation: >-
      Quantifies the autosomal recessive share of molecularly diagnosed genetic
      DEE cases, contrasting with its larger share of the gene count.
- name: X-linked inheritance
  inheritance_term:
    preferred_term: X-linked inheritance
    term:
      id: HP:0001417
      label: X-linked inheritance
  description: >-
    A small number of genetic DEE genes are X-linked, including CDKL5, PCDH19,
    and ARX, together accounting for 17% of molecularly diagnosed cases.
    X-linked disease and mosaicism complicate cellular targeting for emerging
    gene therapies. PCDH19 departs from the usual X-linked pattern in that
    heterozygous females are affected while hemizygous males are typically
    unaffected transmitting carriers; that observation is recorded in the
    PCDH19 genetic entry, while its mechanistic explanation (cellular
    interference) is left to the PCDH19 Clustering Epilepsy child entry, since
    no source cached here states it.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39237642
    reference_title: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      with a small number
      following X-linked or mitochondrial inheritance patterns
    explanation: >-
      Establishes X-linked inheritance as a recognized but numerically minor
      mode among DEE genes.
  - reference: PMID:39613335
    reference_title: National survey on the prevalence of single-gene aetiologies for genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathies in Italy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      17%
      (n=271) in X-linked genes
    explanation: >-
      Quantifies the X-linked share of molecularly diagnosed genetic DEE cases.
  - reference: PMID:39237642
    reference_title: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Mosaicism and X-linked disorders further complicate cellular targeting.
    explanation: >-
      Supports the therapeutic-targeting caveat noted for X-linked genetic DEE.
has_subtypes:
- name: DEE6B
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 6B, non-Dravet (SCN1A)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 6B
    term:
      id: MONDO:0030268
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 6B
  genes:
  - preferred_term: SCN1A
    term:
      id: hgnc:10585
      label: SCN1A
  description: 'The non-Dravet pole of SCN1A developmental and epileptic encephalopathy. MONDO treats
    this as a class distinct from both Dravet syndrome and SCN1A DEE6A, and the founding cohort argues
    the same clinically: seizure onset at 6 to 12 weeks, profound developmental impairment with no speech
    and no ambulation, and a hyperkinetic movement disorder with prominent oral dyskinesia, a combination
    the authors describe as readily distinguishable from Dravet syndrome. Eight of the nine children carried
    the recurrent missense variant p.Thr226Met. Dravet syndrome itself is curated as the separate Dravet_syndrome
    entry, and SCN1A is carried in this entry''s genetic section and wired to the ion-channel and synaptic
    lesion node, so this row records only the non-Dravet concept.'
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:28794249
    reference_title: 'Not all SCN1A epileptic encephalopathies are Dravet syndrome: Early profound Thr226Met
      phenotype.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We describe a distinct SCN1A phenotype, early infantile SCN1A encephalopathy, which is readily
      distinguishable from the well-recognized entities of Dravet syndrome and genetic epilepsy with febrile
      seizures plus.
    explanation: Establishes the non-Dravet SCN1A encephalopathy that this subtype term names, and its
      separation from Dravet syndrome.
  - reference: PMID:28794249
    reference_title: 'Not all SCN1A epileptic encephalopathies are Dravet syndrome: Early profound Thr226Met
      phenotype.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Seizure onset was at 6 to 12 weeks with hemiclonic seizures, bilateral tonic-clonic seizures,
      or spasms. All children had profound developmental impairment and were nonverbal and nonambulatory,
      and 7 of 9 required a gastrostomy.
    explanation: Quantifies the onset window and the severity that distinguish this subtype from Dravet
      syndrome.
- name: DEE23
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 23 (DOCK7)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 23
    term:
      id: MONDO:0014371
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 23
  genes:
  - preferred_term: DOCK7
    term:
      id: hgnc:19190
      label: DOCK7
  description: Biallelic truncating DOCK7 variants. The founding report described three girls from
    two nonconsanguineous families with dysmorphic features, early-onset intractable epilepsy, intellectual
    disability and cortical blindness, all compound heterozygous for truncating DOCK7 alleles. DOCK7
    encodes a Rac guanine nucleotide exchange factor implicated in the genesis and polarization of
    newborn pyramidal neurons and in the morphological differentiation of cortical GABAergic interneurons,
    so the lesion is developmental rather than primarily one of channel conduction.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:24814191
    reference_title: Mutations in DOCK7 in individuals with epileptic encephalopathy and cortical
      blindness.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We describe here three girls from two nonconsanguineous families affected by a clinical
      entity characterized by dysmorphic features, early-onset intractable epilepsy, intellectual
      disability, and cortical blindness.
    explanation: Establishes the DEE23 clinical entity, including the cortical blindness that distinguishes
      it.
  - reference: PMID:24814191
    reference_title: Mutations in DOCK7 in individuals with epileptic encephalopathy and cortical
      blindness.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Sanger sequencing confirmed that all three individuals are compound heterozygotes for
      these truncating mutations in DOCK7.
    explanation: Establishes biallelic truncating DOCK7 variants as the lesion defining this subtype.
- name: DEE35
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 35 (ITPA)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 35
    term:
      id: MONDO:0014719
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 35
  genes:
  - preferred_term: ITPA
    term:
      id: hgnc:6176
      label: ITPA
  description: 'Inosine triphosphate pyrophosphohydrolase (ITPase) deficiency, a purine pathway defect.
    Reported as an infantile-onset epileptic encephalopathy with a lethal course: infantile-onset
    neurodegeneration, progressive microcephaly and epilepsy, with cardiomyopathy in 42% of those
    in whom it was explicitly evaluated. This subtype sits in the metabolic rather than the channelopathy
    arm of the DEE umbrella, and MONDO also files it under inborn disorder of purine metabolism.'
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:35098521
    reference_title: 'Neurodegeneration and Early Infantile Epilepsy Associated with ITPA Variants:
      A Case Series and Review of Literature.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Inosine triphosphate pyrophosphohydrolase (ITPase) deficiency associated with mutations
      in the ITPA gene is a recently characterized purine pathway defect that presents with early
      infantile epileptic encephalopathy and lethal course.
    explanation: Establishes ITPA as the causal gene and the early infantile epileptic encephalopathy
      phenotype.
  - reference: PMID:35098521
    reference_title: 'Neurodegeneration and Early Infantile Epilepsy Associated with ITPA Variants:
      A Case Series and Review of Literature.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: ITPA-related encephalopathy presents with infantile-onset neurodegeneration, progressive
      microcephaly, and epilepsy.
    explanation: Supports the microcephaly and neurodegenerative course recorded for this subtype.
  - reference: PMID:35098521
    reference_title: 'Neurodegeneration and Early Infantile Epilepsy Associated with ITPA Variants:
      A Case Series and Review of Literature.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Cardiomyopathy was noted in 42% of patients where it was explicitly evaluated (n = 5/12).
    explanation: Source for the cardiomyopathy figure recorded in this subtype's description.
- name: DEE36
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 36 (ALG13)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 36
    term:
      id: MONDO:0010472
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 36
  genes:
  - preferred_term: ALG13
    term:
      id: hgnc:30881
      label: ALG13
  description: X-linked ALG13-related DEE, in almost all reported cases caused by the recurrent de
    novo missense variant p.(Asn107Ser). In a 38-individual series 37 were girls and one was a boy.
    It usually manifests as West syndrome with severe to profound developmental delay. Transferrin
    electrophoresis is normal in most cases, and the cited series leaves open whether this is genuinely
    a congenital disorder of glycosylation, which is how MONDO classifies it.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33410528
    reference_title: The phenotypic spectrum of X-linked, infantile onset ALG13-related developmental
      and epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: X-linked ALG13-related DEE usually manifests as West syndrome with severe to profound
      developmental delay. It is predominantly caused by the recurrent de novo missense variant p.(Asn107Ser).
    explanation: Establishes the recurrent de novo ALG13 variant and the West syndrome presentation
      of this subtype.
  - reference: PMID:33410528
    reference_title: The phenotypic spectrum of X-linked, infantile onset ALG13-related developmental
      and epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Comprehensive functional studies will be able to prove or disprove an association with
      congenital disorder of glycosylation.
    explanation: Records that the glycosylation-disorder classification MONDO applies to this term
      is unsettled in the clinical literature.
  - reference: PMID:33410528
    reference_title: The phenotypic spectrum of X-linked, infantile onset ALG13-related developmental
      and epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We delineate the phenotypic spectrum of 38 individuals, 37 girls and one boy, 16 of them
      novel and 22 published, with the most common pathogenic ALG13 variant p.(Asn107Ser) and additionally
      report the phenotype of three individuals carrying other likely pathogenic ALG13 variants.
    explanation: Source for the cohort size and the sex distribution recorded here.
- name: DEE37
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 37 (FRRS1L)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 37
    term:
      id: MONDO:0014859
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 37
  genes:
  - preferred_term: FRRS1L
    term:
      id: hgnc:1362
      label: FRRS1L
  description: Biallelic loss-of-function FRRS1L variants. FRRS1L encodes an AMPA receptor outer-core
    protein, and its loss attenuates AMPA-mediated currents, so this is a postsynaptic glutamatergic
    lesion. The reported phenotype couples epilepsy with prominent choreoathetosis, which is why the
    founding report called it an epileptic-dyskinetic encephalopathy.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:27236917
    reference_title: Loss-of-Function Mutations in FRRS1L Lead to an Epileptic-Dyskinetic Encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We describe a neurological disorder with epilepsy and prominent choreoathetosis caused
      by biallelic pathogenic variants in FRRS1L, which encodes an AMPA receptor outer-core protein.
    explanation: Establishes biallelic FRRS1L variants and the epileptic-dyskinetic phenotype of this
      subtype.
  - reference: PMID:27236917
    reference_title: Loss-of-Function Mutations in FRRS1L Lead to an Epileptic-Dyskinetic Encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Loss of FRRS1L function attenuates AMPA-mediated currents, implicating chronic abnormalities
      of glutamatergic neurotransmission in this monogenic neurological disease of childhood.
    explanation: Supports placing the FRRS1L lesion in the synaptic arm of the DEE mechanism.
- name: DEE48
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 48 (AP3B2)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 48
    term:
      id: MONDO:0015000
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 48
  genes:
  - preferred_term: AP3B2
    term:
      id: hgnc:567
      label: AP3B2
  description: Biallelic AP3B2 variants. AP3B2 encodes the neuron-specific beta subunit of the AP-3 vesicle
    coat adaptor complex; the ubiquitous isoform AP3B1 causes Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome type 2 instead,
    so the neuronal restriction of this subunit is what makes the AP3B2 phenotype purely neurological.
    Reverse phenotyping of twelve affected individuals from eight families gave a homogeneous early-onset
    epileptic encephalopathy with severe developmental delay, optic atrophy and postnatal microcephaly,
    and no albinism or haematological involvement.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:27889060
    reference_title: Autosomal-Recessive Mutations in AP3B2, Adaptor-Related Protein Complex 3 Beta 2
      Subunit, Cause an Early-Onset Epileptic Encephalopathy with Optic Atrophy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Reverse phenotyping of 12 affected individuals from eight families revealed a homogeneous
      EOEE phenotype characterized by severe developmental delay, poor visual contact with optic atrophy,
      and postnatal microcephaly.
    explanation: Establishes the DEE48 clinical entity and the optic atrophy that characterises it.
  - reference: PMID:27889060
    reference_title: Autosomal-Recessive Mutations in AP3B2, Adaptor-Related Protein Complex 3 Beta 2
      Subunit, Cause an Early-Onset Epileptic Encephalopathy with Optic Atrophy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Among a cohort of 57 individuals with epileptic encephalopathy, we ascertained two unrelated
      affected individuals with EOEE associated with developmental impairment and autosomal-recessive
      variants in AP3B2 by means of whole-exome sequencing.
    explanation: Establishes autosomal-recessive AP3B2 variants as the lesion defining this subtype.
- name: DEE51
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 51 (MDH2)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 51
    term:
      id: MONDO:0015025
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 51
  genes:
  - preferred_term: MDH2
    term:
      id: hgnc:6971
      label: MDH2
  description: Biallelic MDH2 variants, a Krebs cycle defect. MDH2 encodes mitochondrial malate dehydrogenase,
    which converts malate to oxaloacetate. The three unrelated subjects of the founding report had early-onset
    generalised hypotonia, psychomotor delay and refractory epilepsy with raised lactate in blood and
    cerebrospinal fluid; their fibroblasts showed loss of MDH2 protein with enzymatic activity close to
    null, and accumulation of malate and fumarate. The lesion is therefore metabolic rather than one of
    channel conduction, which is why this subtype gene is wired to the non-channelopathy lesion node.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:27989324
    reference_title: Mutations in MDH2, Encoding a Krebs Cycle Enzyme, Cause Early-Onset Severe Encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We report bi-allelic pathogenic mutations in MDH2 in three unrelated subjects presenting
      with early-onset generalized hypotonia, psychomotor delay, refractory epilepsy, and elevated lactate
      in the blood and cerebrospinal fluid.
    explanation: Establishes the DEE51 clinical entity and biallelic MDH2 variants as its lesion.
  - reference: PMID:27989324
    reference_title: Mutations in MDH2, Encoding a Krebs Cycle Enzyme, Cause Early-Onset Severe Encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: Functional studies in fibroblasts from affected subjects showed both an apparently complete
      loss of MDH2 levels and MDH2 enzymatic activity close to null.
    explanation: Shows the lesion abolishes malate dehydrogenase activity, which is the mechanism this
      subtype contributes.
- name: DEE53
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 53 (SYNJ1)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 53
    term:
      id: MONDO:0033362
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 53
  genes:
  - preferred_term: SYNJ1
    term:
      id: hgnc:11503
      label: SYNJ1
  description: 'Biallelic SYNJ1 variants. SYNJ1 encodes synaptojanin 1, a polyphosphoinositide phosphatase
    with two consecutive phosphatase domains that acts in synaptic vesicle dynamics. The allelic series
    separates two diseases: variants that selectively abolish only the Sac1 domain cause early-onset parkinsonism,
    whereas a critical reduction of the dual phosphatase activity causes this neonatal refractory epilepsy
    with progressive neurological decline. A screen of 543 further patients with epilepsy and intellectual
    disability found no additional pathogenic variants, so SYNJ1 deficiency is rare and tied to a specific
    phenotype.'
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:27435091
    reference_title: Loss of SYNJ1 dual phosphatase activity leads to early onset refractory seizures
      and progressive neurological decline.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We performed whole exome or genome sequencing in three independent sib pairs with early onset
      refractory seizures and progressive neurological decline, and identified novel segregating recessive
      SYNJ1 defects.
    explanation: Establishes the DEE53 clinical entity and recessive SYNJ1 variants as its lesion.
  - reference: PMID:27435091
    reference_title: Loss of SYNJ1 dual phosphatase activity leads to early onset refractory seizures
      and progressive neurological decline.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: A genetic follow-up screening in a large cohort of 543 patients with a wide phenotypical
      range of epilepsies and intellectual disability revealed no additional pathogenic variants, showing
      that SYNJ1 deficiency is rare and probably linked to a specific phenotype.
    explanation: Sources the rarity and phenotypic specificity stated in this row description.
- name: DEE57
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 57 (KCNT2)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 57
    term:
      id: MONDO:0033366
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 57
  genes:
  - preferred_term: KCNT2
    term:
      id: hgnc:18866
      label: KCNT2
  description: De novo KCNT2 variants. KCNT2 encodes a sodium-activated potassium channel subunit of the
    same subfamily as KCNT1. The two girls of the founding report had West syndrome evolving to Lennox-Gastaut
    syndrome in one and epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures in the other. In vitro analysis
    indicated quinidine-responsive gain of function, and quinidine add-on therapy produced marked clinical
    improvement in one of them, so this subtype shares the pharmacological profile as well as the phenotype
    of KCNT1-related disease.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29740868
    reference_title: De novo gain-of-function variants in KCNT2 as a novel cause of developmental and
      epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We report on 2 females with de novo variants in KCNT2 with West syndrome followed by Lennox-Gastaut
      syndrome or with DEE with migrating focal seizures.
    explanation: Establishes the DEE57 clinical entity and de novo KCNT2 variants as its lesion.
  - reference: PMID:29740868
    reference_title: De novo gain-of-function variants in KCNT2 as a novel cause of developmental and
      epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: After in vitro analysis suggested quinidine-responsive gain-of-function effects, we treated
      1 of the girls with quinidine add-on therapy and achieved marked clinical improvements.
    explanation: Sources both the gain-of-function mechanism and the quinidine response stated in this
      row description.
- name: DEE58
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 58 (NTRK2)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 58
    term:
      id: MONDO:0033367
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 58
  genes:
  - preferred_term: NTRK2
    term:
      id: hgnc:8032
      label: NTRK2
  description: NTRK2-related DEE, reported with a recurrent variant in four of the five cases in the
    cited series. The phenotype is early-onset seizures beginning as infantile spasms and later evolving
    to multifocal seizures, with global developmental delay, variable movement disorders, microcephaly
    and optic nerve hypoplasia. HGNC names NTRK2 neurotrophic receptor tyrosine kinase 2, with TRKB
    as an alias symbol, so the lesion is in receptor signalling rather than in channel conduction.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34425480
    reference_title: 'NTRK2-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy: Report of 5 new cases.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Five cases of NTRK2-related DEE were identified. Four had a previously described recurrent
      variant in NTRK2 and one had a novel variant.
    explanation: Establishes NTRK2 as the causal gene of this subtype and the recurrence of one variant.
  - reference: PMID:34425480
    reference_title: 'NTRK2-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy: Report of 5 new cases.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: The phenotype was characterized by early-onset seizures (infantile spasms, later evolving
      to multifocal seizures), global developmental delay, variable movement disorders, microcephaly
      and optic nerve hypoplasia.
    explanation: Source for the seizure evolution, microcephaly and optic nerve hypoplasia recorded
      here.
- name: DEE59
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 59 (GABBR2)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 59
    term:
      id: MONDO:0033368
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 59
  genes:
  - preferred_term: GABBR2
    term:
      id: hgnc:4507
      label: GABBR2
  description: De novo GABBR2 variants. GABBR2 encodes the type 2 subunit of the metabotropic GABA-B receptor,
    so this subtype sits with the GABA-A receptor subunit subtypes as a lesion of GABAergic inhibition
    rather than of a voltage-gated channel. De novo GABBR2 mutations were reported in two individuals
    in the combined EuroEPINOMICS and Epi4K/EPGP trio cohort, which treated them as suggestive rather
    than statistically established; a later whole-genome study of unexplained DEE provided the causal
    link.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25262651
    reference_title: De novo mutations in synaptic transmission genes including DNM1 cause epileptic encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: In this expanded cohort, we find 429 de novo mutations, including de novo mutations in DNM1
      in five individuals and de novo mutations in GABBR2, FASN, and RYR3 in two individuals each.
    explanation: The first observation of de novo GABBR2 mutations in a DEE trio cohort, which is the
      report OMIM cites for DEE59.
  - reference: PMID:25262651
    reference_title: De novo mutations in synaptic transmission genes including DNM1 cause epileptic encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We bring statistical evidence that mutations in DNM1 cause epileptic encephalopathy, find
      suggestive evidence for a role of three additional genes, and show that at least 12% of analyzed
      individuals have an identifiable causal de novo mutation.
    explanation: Sources the statement that the first report treated GABBR2 as suggestive rather than
      established; the statistical evidence in that paper is for DNM1, not for GABBR2.
  - reference: PMID:29100083
    reference_title: High Rate of Recurrent De Novo Mutations in Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: 'By combining these strategies, we were able to provide a causal link between DEE and the
      following genes: NTRK2, GABRB2, CLTC, DHDDS, NUS1, RAB11A, GABBR2, and SNAP25.'
    explanation: Establishes GABBR2 as causal for DEE. The sentence names eight genes, so it supports
      gene-disease causality for each named gene and no gene-specific phenotype claim.
- name: DEE60
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 60 (CNPY3)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 60
    term:
      id: MONDO:0033369
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 60
  genes:
  - preferred_term: CNPY3
    term:
      id: hgnc:11968
      label: CNPY3
  description: Biallelic CNPY3 variants. CNPY3 encodes an endoplasmic reticulum co-chaperone that regulates
    the subcellular distribution and responses of multiple Toll-like receptors, a function outside the
    channel and synaptic classes. The three individuals of the founding report presented as West syndrome
    and all three had hippocampal malrotation; CNPY3 protein was severely reduced in lymphoblastoid cells
    from two of them. Cnpy3-knockout mice showed spastic or dystonic features at rest and enhanced resting
    EEG activity in the fast beta band, which the authors suggest could mimic the fast waves seen in those
    two individuals.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29394991
    reference_title: Biallelic Variants in CNPY3, Encoding an Endoplasmic Reticulum Chaperone, Cause Early-Onset
      Epileptic Encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We have now identified biallelic CNPY3 variants in three individuals with WS; these include
      compound-heterozygous missense and frameshift variants in a family with two affected siblings (individuals
      1 and 2) and a homozygous splicing variant in a consanguineous family (individual 3).
    explanation: Establishes the DEE60 clinical entity, presenting as West syndrome, and biallelic CNPY3
      variants as its lesion.
  - reference: PMID:29394991
    reference_title: Biallelic Variants in CNPY3, Encoding an Endoplasmic Reticulum Chaperone, Cause Early-Onset
      Epileptic Encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: Cnpy3-knockout mice exhibited spastic or dystonic features under resting conditions and hyperactivity
      and anxiolytic behavior during the open field test.
    explanation: Model-organism support for CNPY3 loss producing a neurological phenotype.
- name: DEE61
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 61 (ADAM22)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 61
    term:
      id: MONDO:0033370
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 61
  genes:
  - preferred_term: ADAM22
    term:
      id: hgnc:201
      label: ADAM22
  description: 'Biallelic inactivating ADAM22 variants. ADAM22 is the postsynaptic receptor for the
    secreted protein LGI1, and this subtype is the recessive counterpart of the dominant LGI1 epilepsy
    with auditory features. All affected individuals in the cited series had infantile-onset treatment-resistant
    epilepsy. Transfected-cell studies indicated three distinct pathological mechanisms: defective
    cell-membrane expression, impaired LGI1 binding, and impaired interaction with the postsynaptic
    density protein PSD-95.'
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:35373813
    reference_title: Biallelic ADAM22 pathogenic variants cause progressive encephalopathy and infantile-onset
      refractory epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We refine the phenotype and report 19 additional individuals harbouring compound heterozygous
      or homozygous inactivating ADAM22 variants, of whom 18 had clinical data available.
    explanation: Establishes biallelic inactivating ADAM22 variants in a cohort, defining this subtype.
  - reference: PMID:35373813
    reference_title: Biallelic ADAM22 pathogenic variants cause progressive encephalopathy and infantile-onset
      refractory epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: All affected individuals exhibited infantile-onset, treatment-resistant epilepsy.
    explanation: Source for the uniform infantile-onset drug-resistant epilepsy recorded here.
  - reference: PMID:35373813
    reference_title: Biallelic ADAM22 pathogenic variants cause progressive encephalopathy and infantile-onset
      refractory epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: 'Functional studies in transfected cell lines confirmed the deleteriousness of all identified
      variants and indicated at least three distinct pathological mechanisms: (i) defective cell membrane
      expression; (ii) impaired LGI1-binding; and/or (iii) impaired interaction with the postsynaptic
      density protein PSD-95.'
    explanation: Source for the three molecular consequences of ADAM22 loss recorded here.
- name: DEE62
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 62 (SCN3A)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 62
    term:
      id: MONDO:0033371
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 62
  genes:
  - preferred_term: SCN3A
    term:
      id: hgnc:10590
      label: SCN3A
  description: De novo SCN3A variants. SCN3A encodes the Nav1.3 sodium channel alpha subunit, highly expressed
    in brain and, before this report, not linked to early infantile epileptic encephalopathy. The four
    patients carried heterozygous de novo missense variants, and recordings showed gain of channel function
    with a markedly increased slowly inactivating current; phenytoin and lacosamide blocked that slowly
    inactivating component selectively, which is the pharmacological lead the authors draw from the mechanism.
    Variants known or presumed to be inherited did not show gain of function.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29466837
    reference_title: Mutations in SCN3A cause early infantile epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Here, we describe a cohort of 4 patients with epileptic encephalopathy and heterozygous de
      novo missense variants in SCN3A (p.Ile875Thr in 2 cases, p.Pro1333Leu, and p.Val1769Ala).
    explanation: Establishes the DEE62 clinical entity and de novo SCN3A missense variants as its lesion.
  - reference: PMID:29466837
    reference_title: Mutations in SCN3A cause early infantile epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: Electrophysiological recordings of mutant channels revealed prominent gain of channel function,
      with a markedly increased amplitude of the slowly inactivating current component
    explanation: Sources the gain-of-function mechanism stated in this row description.
- name: DEE67
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 67 (CUX2)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 67
    term:
      id: MONDO:0029138
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 67
  genes:
  - preferred_term: CUX2
    term:
      id: hgnc:19347
      label: CUX2
  description: The recurrent de novo CUX2 p.Glu590Lys variant. CUX2 is a cut homeodomain transcription
    factor with a role in dendrite branching, spine development and synapse formation in layer II to III
    cortical neurons, so the lesion is transcriptional rather than a channel or synaptic protein defect
    and the gene is wired to the non-channelopathy lesion node. The nine-patient cohort spans a phenotypic
    range with infantile-onset myoclonic DEE at the severe end and generalised epilepsy with severe static
    developmental encephalopathy at the milder end; the variant affects a highly conserved residue in
    the CUT domain predicted to interfere with DNA binding.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29630738
    reference_title: The epilepsy phenotypic spectrum associated with a recurrent CUX2 variant.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We identify a recurrent de novo CUX2 p.Glu590Lys as a novel genetic cause for developmental
      and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE).
    explanation: Establishes the DEE67 clinical entity and the recurrent CUX2 variant as its lesion.
  - reference: PMID:29630738
    reference_title: The epilepsy phenotypic spectrum associated with a recurrent CUX2 variant.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Patients with CUX2 p.Glu590Lys display a distinctive phenotypic spectrum, which is predominantly
      generalized epilepsy, with infantile-onset myoclonic DEE at the severe end and generalized epilepsy
      with severe static developmental encephalopathy at the milder end of the spectrum.
    explanation: Sources the severity range stated in this row description.
- name: DEE68
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 68 (TRAK1)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 68
    term:
      id: MONDO:0032598
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 68
  genes:
  - preferred_term: TRAK1
    term:
      id: hgnc:29947
      label: TRAK1
  description: Biallelic truncating TRAK1 variants. The founding report identified a homozygous splice
    variant in six lethal encephalopathic patients from three unrelated families; patient-derived
    fibroblasts showed irregular mitochondrial distribution, altered mitochondrial motility, reduced
    membrane potential and diminished respiration. Note that the founding report frames the phenotype
    as a fatal encephalopathy rather than using the DEE label that OMIM 618201 and MONDO later attached
    to this locus.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:28364549
    reference_title: Deleterious variants in TRAK1 disrupt mitochondrial movement and cause fatal
      encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Using whole exome sequencing, we identified homozygous truncating variants in TRAK1 (NM_001042646:c.287-2A
      > C), in six lethal encephalopathic patients from three unrelated families.
    explanation: Establishes the biallelic TRAK1 lesion and the lethal encephalopathic phenotype of
      this subtype.
  - reference: PMID:28364549
    reference_title: Deleterious variants in TRAK1 disrupt mitochondrial movement and cause fatal
      encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: In comparison with normal cells, TRAK1-deficient fibroblasts showed irregular mitochondrial
      distribution, altered mitochondrial motility, reduced mitochondrial membrane potential, and
      diminished mitochondrial respiration.
    explanation: Source for the mitochondrial trafficking and respiration defect; the measurements
      are in patient-derived fibroblasts.
- name: DEE70
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 70 (PHACTR1)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 70
    term:
      id: MONDO:0032663
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 70
  genes:
  - preferred_term: PHACTR1
    term:
      id: hgnc:20990
      label: PHACTR1
  description: De novo PHACTR1 variants, whose founding report is titled for their identification
    in West syndrome. Immunoprecipitation showed that the disease variants impair either PHACTR1's
    actin-binding activity or its binding to protein phosphatase 1. In a later nine-patient series
    eight individuals carried missense variants and one a copy-number variant; infantile epileptic
    spasms syndrome was the unifying phenotype of the eight with missense variants, while the copy-number
    patient had a developmental encephalopathy phenotype instead.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:38272663
    reference_title: Genotype and phenotype correlation of PHACTR1-related neurological disorders.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Infantile epileptic spasms syndrome (IESS) was the unifying phenotype in eight patients
      with missense variants of PHACTR1.
    explanation: Establishes epileptic spasms as the core phenotype of PHACTR1 missense variants,
      in the largest reported series.
  - reference: PMID:38272663
    reference_title: Genotype and phenotype correlation of PHACTR1-related neurological disorders.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Patients with variants in PHACTR1 can have a phenotype of developmental encephalopathy
      in addition to IESS.
    explanation: Source for the developmental encephalopathy phenotype recorded alongside epileptic
      spasms in this subtype.
  - reference: PMID:30256902
    reference_title: De novo PHACTR1 mutations in West syndrome and their pathophysiological effects.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: Immunoprecipitation analyses revealed that actin-binding activity of PHACTR1 was impaired
      by the p.Leu500Pro, p.Asn479Ile and p.Ile518Asn mutations while the p.Arg521Cys mutation exhibited
      impaired binding to PP1.
    explanation: Establishes the two molecular consequences of the disease variants, in transfected-cell
      immunoprecipitation assays.
- name: DEE73
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 73 (RNF13)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 73
    term:
      id: MONDO:0034106
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 73
  genes:
  - preferred_term: RNF13
    term:
      id: hgnc:10057
      label: RNF13
  description: De novo heterozygous gain-of-function RNF13 variants. Three unrelated individuals presented
    with congenital microcephaly, infantile epileptic encephalopathy and profound developmental delay.
    RNF13 interacts with the unfolded-protein-response sensor IRE1-alpha, and the variants act by
    increasing signalling through the ER stress response rather than by haploinsufficiency.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:30595371
    reference_title: Heterozygous RNF13 Gain-of-Function Variants Are Associated with Congenital Microcephaly,
      Epileptic Encephalopathy, Blindness, and Failure to Thrive.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Three unrelated affected individuals with congenital microcephaly, infantile epileptic
      encephalopathy, and profound developmental delay were found to carry heterozygous variants
    explanation: Establishes the three-patient founding cohort and the congenital microcephaly plus
      infantile epileptic encephalopathy phenotype.
  - reference: PMID:30595371
    reference_title: Heterozygous RNF13 Gain-of-Function Variants Are Associated with Congenital Microcephaly,
      Epileptic Encephalopathy, Blindness, and Failure to Thrive.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: These results indicate that the RNF13 variants confer gain of function to the encoded
      protein and thereby lead to altered signaling of the ER stress response associated with severe
      neurodegeneration in infancy.
    explanation: Establishes the gain-of-function mechanism acting through the ER stress response.
- name: DEE75
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 75 (PARS2)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 75
    term:
      id: MONDO:0032752
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 75
  genes:
  - preferred_term: PARS2
    term:
      id: hgnc:30563
      label: PARS2
  description: 'Biallelic PARS2 variants. PARS2 encodes mitochondrial prolyl-tRNA synthetase, one
    of the mitochondrial aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, and had first been linked to Alpers syndrome
    and infantile-onset neurodegeneration. Reported patients have epileptic spasms with an early treatment
    response, early developmental delay or regression, generalised hypotonia, postnatal microcephaly,
    elevated lactate and progressive cerebral atrophy. A nomenclature hazard is recorded on the NEUROD2-Related_Developmental_and_Epileptic_Encephalopathy
    entry: a publication cited there misapplies the DEE75 number to NEUROD2, which is DEE72.'
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29915213
    reference_title: The genotypic and phenotypic spectrum of PARS2-related infantile-onset encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: As a member of the mt-aaRS family, PARS2 encoding prolyl-tRNA synthetase 2 was recently
      shown to be associated with Alpers syndrome and certain infantile-onset neurodegenerative disorders
      in four patients.
    explanation: Establishes PARS2 as a mitochondrial aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase gene causing infantile-onset
      encephalopathy.
  - reference: PMID:29915213
    reference_title: The genotypic and phenotypic spectrum of PARS2-related infantile-onset encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Nearly all patients had epileptic spasms with early response to treatment, early developmental
      delay and/or regression followed by generalized hypotonia, postnatal microcephaly, elevated
      lactate levels, and progressive cerebral atrophy.
    explanation: Source for the epileptic spasms, microcephaly, lactate elevation and cerebral atrophy
      recorded here.
- name: DEE76
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 76 (ACTL6B)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 76
    term:
      id: MONDO:0032768
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 76
  genes:
  - preferred_term: ACTL6B
    term:
      id: hgnc:160
      label: ACTL6B
  description: Biallelic ACTL6B variants. ACTL6B encodes a subunit of the neuron-specific chromatin
    remodelling complex nBAF, which is the chromatin-regulator arm of the ion-channel and synaptic
    lesion node this subtype is wired to rather than a channel or synaptic protein in its own right.
    The two siblings in whom the gene was identified had severe DEE with microcephaly,
    spastic tetraplegia, diffuse brain hypomyelination, cerebellar atrophy, short stature and kyphoscoliosis;
    the founding report describes three cases in total.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:30656450
    reference_title: Mutations in ACTL6B, coding for a subunit of the neuron-specific chromatin remodeling
      complex nBAF, cause early onset severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with brain
      hypomyelination and cerebellar atrophy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: In this study, we investigated the genetic defects in two siblings who presented with
      severe DEE, microcephaly, spastic tetraplegia, diffuse brain hypomyelination, cerebellar atrophy,
      short stature, and kyphoscoliosis.
    explanation: Source for the DEE76 phenotype recorded here, including the hypomyelination and cerebellar
      atrophy.
  - reference: PMID:30656450
    reference_title: Mutations in ACTL6B, coding for a subunit of the neuron-specific chromatin remodeling
      complex nBAF, cause early onset severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with brain
      hypomyelination and cerebellar atrophy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Whole exome next-generation sequencing (WES) identified in both siblings a homozygous
      non-sense variant in the ACTL6B gene
    explanation: Establishes the biallelic ACTL6B lesion defining this subtype.
- name: DEE78
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 78 (GABRA2)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 78
    term:
      id: MONDO:0032812
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 78
  genes:
  - preferred_term: GABRA2
    term:
      id: hgnc:4076
      label: GABRA2
  description: A de novo GABRA2 variant. GABRA2 encodes the alpha2 subunit of the GABA-A receptor, a ligand-gated
    anion channel that regulates neuronal inhibition. The p.Thr292Lys variant was found by targeted resequencing
    of 279 epilepsy patients, in a patient with severe epilepsy and developmental delay. Patch-clamp recordings
    showed it reduced channel expression and produced channels that were tonically open even without GABA,
    so the receptor lesion is not a simple loss of GABA response. DEE78 and DEE79 were established together
    in this one study.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29961870
    reference_title: De novo variants in GABRA2 and GABRA5 alter receptor function and contribute to early-onset
      epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Targeted resequencing of 279 additional epilepsy patients identified 19 rare variants from
      nine GABAA receptor genes, including a novel de novo missense variant in GABRA2 (c.875C > A, p.T292K)
      and a recurrent missense variant in GABRB3 (c.902C > T, p.P301L).
    explanation: Establishes the de novo GABRA2 variant that defines this subtype and how it was ascertained.
  - reference: PMID:29961870
    reference_title: De novo variants in GABRA2 and GABRA5 alter receptor function and contribute to early-onset
      epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: The GABRA2 p.T292K variant reduced channel expression and produced mutant channels that were
      tonically open, even in the absence of GABA.
    explanation: Gene-specific functional characterisation of the GABRA2 lesion, measured in transfected
      HEK293T cells.
- name: DEE79
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 79 (GABRA5)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 79
    term:
      id: MONDO:0032813
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 79
  genes:
  - preferred_term: GABRA5
    term:
      id: hgnc:4079
      label: GABRA5
  description: A de novo GABRA5 variant. GABRA5 encodes the alpha5 subunit of the GABA-A receptor. The
    index patient was found by whole-genome sequencing and had severe early-onset epilepsy with developmental
    delay. The p.Val294Leu variant produced receptors ten times more sensitive to GABA but with a reduced
    maximal GABA-evoked current because of increased desensitisation, so the net effect is a loss of sustained
    inhibition despite the increased apparent affinity. DEE78 and DEE79 were established together in this
    one study.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29961870
    reference_title: De novo variants in GABRA2 and GABRA5 alter receptor function and contribute to early-onset
      epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Using whole-genome sequencing, we identified a novel de novo missense variant in GABRA5 (c.880G
      > C, p.V294L) in a patient with severe early-onset epilepsy and developmental delay.
    explanation: Establishes the DEE79 clinical entity and the de novo GABRA5 variant as its lesion.
  - reference: PMID:29961870
    reference_title: De novo variants in GABRA2 and GABRA5 alter receptor function and contribute to early-onset
      epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: The GABRA5 p.V294L variant produced receptors that were 10-times more sensitive to GABA but
      had reduced maximal GABA-evoked current due to increased receptor desensitization.
    explanation: Gene-specific functional characterisation of the GABRA5 lesion, measured in transfected
      HEK293T cells.
- name: DEE85
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 85, with or without midline brain defects (SMC1A)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 85, with or without midline brain defects
    term:
      id: MONDO:0026771
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 85, with or without midline brain defects
  genes:
  - preferred_term: SMC1A
    term:
      id: hgnc:11111
      label: SMC1A
  description: 'Heterozygous de novo truncating SMC1A variants, X-linked. SMC1A encodes a core structural
    subunit of the cohesin complex, so this is a cohesinopathy and the gene is wired to the non-channelopathy
    lesion node. The allelic split matters clinically: missense and small in-frame SMC1A changes cause
    about 5 per cent of Cornelia de Lange syndrome, which dismech curates separately, whereas protein-truncating
    changes cause this epilepsy phenotype. All ten cases of the defining series were female, none had
    a clinical diagnosis of Cornelia de Lange syndrome, and the striking feature was seizures occurring
    in clusters associated with developmental regression.'
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:28166369
    reference_title: 'Heterozygous truncation mutations of the SMC1A gene cause a severe early onset epilepsy
      with cluster seizures in females: Detailed phenotyping of 10 new cases.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Ten cases with heterozygous de novo mutations in the SMC1A gene are presented. All 10 mutations
      identified are predicted to result in premature truncation of the SMC1A protein.
    explanation: Establishes truncating SMC1A variants as the lesion defining this subtype.
  - reference: PMID:28166369
    reference_title: 'Heterozygous truncation mutations of the SMC1A gene cause a severe early onset epilepsy
      with cluster seizures in females: Detailed phenotyping of 10 new cases.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: All cases are female, and none had a clinical diagnosis of CdLS.
    explanation: Sources the separation of this subtype from Cornelia de Lange syndrome, which is curated
      as its own dismech entry.
  - reference: PMID:28166369
    reference_title: 'Heterozygous truncation mutations of the SMC1A gene cause a severe early onset epilepsy
      with cluster seizures in females: Detailed phenotyping of 10 new cases.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: In the majority of cases, a marked preponderance for seizures to occur in clusters was noted.
      Seizure clusters were associated with developmental regression.
    explanation: Sources the cluster-seizure pattern and its link to regression stated in this row description.
- name: DEE86
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 86 (DALRD3)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 86
    term:
      id: MONDO:0030054
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 86
  genes:
  - preferred_term: DALRD3
    term:
      id: hgnc:25536
      label: DALRD3
  description: A homozygous nonsense DALRD3 variant. DALRD3 forms a complex with the METTL2 methyltransferase
    that recognises particular arginine tRNA isoacceptors for 3-methylcytosine modification of the anticodon
    loop, and DALRD3-deficient human cells lose that modification almost completely. The lesion is therefore
    in tRNA modification, placing this subtype with the non-channelopathy mechanisms.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:32427860
    reference_title: DALRD3 encodes a protein mutated in epileptic encephalopathy that targets arginine
      tRNAs for 3-methylcytosine modification.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Notably, we identify a homozygous nonsense mutation in the DALRD3 gene that impairs m3C formation
      in human patients exhibiting developmental delay and early-onset epileptic encephalopathy.
    explanation: Establishes the DEE86 clinical entity and the homozygous DALRD3 lesion, together with
      the tRNA-modification defect it causes.
  - reference: PMID:32427860
    reference_title: DALRD3 encodes a protein mutated in epileptic encephalopathy that targets arginine
      tRNAs for 3-methylcytosine modification.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: DALRD3-deficient human cells exhibit nearly complete loss of the m3C modification in tRNA-Arg
      species.
    explanation: Sources the molecular consequence of DALRD3 loss stated in this row description.
- name: DEE90
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 90 (FGF13)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 90
    term:
      id: MONDO:0025353
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 90
  genes:
  - preferred_term: FGF13
    term:
      id: hgnc:3670
      label: FGF13
  description: X-linked DEE caused by missense variants in the N-terminal domain of the A isoform
    of FHF2, the protein encoded by FGF13. Fibroblast growth factor homologous factors are intracellular
    regulators of voltage-gated sodium channels. Mutant FHF2A co-expressed with wild-type Nav1.6 lost
    the ability to induce rapid-onset, long-term blockade of the channel while retaining pro-excitatory
    properties, a gain-of-function effect on excitability. Affected individuals - two sibling pairs
    and three unrelated males - had intractable focal seizures and severe developmental delay from
    infancy.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33245860
    reference_title: Missense variants in the N-terminal domain of the A isoform of FHF2/FGF13 cause
      an X-linked developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Here, we describe two sibling pairs and three unrelated males who presented in infancy
      with intractable focal seizures and severe developmental delay. Whole-exome sequencing identified
      hemi- and heterozygous variants in the N-terminal domain of the A isoform of FHF2 (FHF2A).
    explanation: Establishes the founding cohort and the FHF2A N-terminal variants defining this subtype.
  - reference: PMID:33245860
    reference_title: Missense variants in the N-terminal domain of the A isoform of FHF2/FGF13 cause
      an X-linked developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Our findings demonstrate that FHF2 variants are a cause of infantile-onset developmental
      and epileptic encephalopathy and underline the critical role of the FHF2A isoform in regulating
      Nav channel function.
    explanation: States the gene-disease relationship and the sodium-channel regulatory mechanism
      that places this lesion in the channel arm.
  - reference: PMID:33245860
    reference_title: Missense variants in the N-terminal domain of the A isoform of FHF2/FGF13 cause
      an X-linked developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: Functional characterization of mutant FHF2A co-expressed with wild-type Nav1.6 (SCN8A)
      revealed that mutant FHF2A proteins lost the ability to induce rapid-onset, long-term blockade
      of the channel while retaining pro-excitatory properties.
    explanation: Source for the gain-of-function effect on sodium-channel inactivation recorded here.
- name: DEE92
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 92 (GABRB2)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 92
    term:
      id: MONDO:0020631
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 92
  genes:
  - preferred_term: GABRB2
    term:
      id: hgnc:4082
      label: GABRB2
  description: De novo GABRB2 variants. GABRB2 encodes the beta2 subunit of the GABA-A receptor. GABRB2
    was one of eight genes given a causal link to DEE by a whole-genome sequencing study of 197 trios
    with unexplained DEE and pharmaco-resistant seizures, combined with targeted sequencing and de-novo-mutation
    enrichment meta-analysis. That study reports gene-disease causality for the set of eight; it does
    not characterise a GABRB2-specific phenotype, so none is asserted here.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29100083
    reference_title: High Rate of Recurrent De Novo Mutations in Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: 'By combining these strategies, we were able to provide a causal link between DEE and the
      following genes: NTRK2, GABRB2, CLTC, DHDDS, NUS1, RAB11A, GABBR2, and SNAP25.'
    explanation: Establishes GABRB2 as causal for DEE. The sentence names eight genes, so it supports
      gene-disease causality for each named gene and no gene-specific phenotype claim.
  - reference: PMID:29100083
    reference_title: High Rate of Recurrent De Novo Mutations in Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We performed whole-genome sequencing (WGS) in 197 individuals with unexplained DEE and pharmaco-resistant
      seizures and in their unaffected parents.
    explanation: Sources the cohort and design behind that causal link.
- name: DEE93
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 93 (ATP6V1A)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 93
    term:
      id: MONDO:0020632
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 93
  genes:
  - preferred_term: ATP6V1A
    term:
      id: hgnc:851
      label: ATP6V1A
  description: 'De novo heterozygous ATP6V1A variants. ATP6V1A encodes the A subunit of the vacuolar proton
    ATPase, the multi-subunit pump that sets organellar pH in all eukaryotic cells and has additional
    roles at the synapse in neurons. Severity in the four founding patients was strikingly variable and
    tracked the variant: two progressed to profound delay with hypotonic or dyskinetic quadriparesis and
    intractable seizures, while two had moderate delay with milder epilepsy. Modelling on v-ATPase structures
    predicted four different mechanisms for the four variants, from perturbed subunit interaction to impaired
    rotation.'
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29668857
    reference_title: De novo mutations of the ATP6V1A gene cause developmental encephalopathy with epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Through whole exome sequencing, we identified de novo heterozygous mutations (p.Pro27Arg,
      p.Asp100Tyr, p.Asp349Asn, p.Asp371Gly) in ATP6V1A, encoding the A subunit of v-ATPase, in four patients
      with developmental encephalopathy with epilepsy.
    explanation: Establishes the DEE93 clinical entity and de novo ATP6V1A variants as its lesion.
  - reference: PMID:29668857
    reference_title: De novo mutations of the ATP6V1A gene cause developmental encephalopathy with epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Early manifestations, observed in all patients, were developmental delay and febrile seizures,
      evolving to encephalopathy with profound delay, hypotonic/dyskinetic quadriparesis and intractable
      multiple seizure types in two patients (p.Pro27Arg, p.Asp100Tyr), and to moderate delay with milder
      epilepsy in the other two (p.Asp349Asn, p.Asp371Gly).
    explanation: Sources the variant-dependent severity range stated in this row description.
- name: DEE96
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 96 (NSF)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 96
    term:
      id: MONDO:0023659
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 96
  genes:
  - preferred_term: NSF
    term:
      id: hgnc:8016
      label: NSF
  description: De novo heterozygous NSF variants. NSF is the homo-hexameric AAA ATPase that acts in membrane
    fusion and in assembly and disassembly of the SNARE complex, so the lesion is in the presynaptic vesicle
    cycle and the gene is wired to the ion-channel and synaptic lesion node alongside NAPB, its own beta
    attachment protein. Expressing the mutant allele in the developing Drosophila eye severely disrupted
    eye development where the wild-type allele did not, which the authors read as a dominant negative
    effect.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:31675180
    reference_title: De novo NSF mutations cause early infantile epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Herein, we, for the first time, document human monogenic disease phenotype of de novo pathogenic
      variants in NSF, that is, epileptic encephalopathy of early infantile onset.
    explanation: Establishes the DEE96 clinical entity and de novo NSF variants as its lesion.
  - reference: PMID:31675180
    reference_title: De novo NSF mutations cause early infantile epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: When expressed in the developing eye of Drosophila, the mutant NSF severely affected eye
      development, while the wild-type allele had no detectable effect under the same conditions.
    explanation: Sources the dominant-negative reading of the NSF lesion stated in this row description.
- name: DEE97
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 97 (CELF2)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 97
    term:
      id: MONDO:0030453
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 97
  genes:
  - preferred_term: CELF2
    term:
      id: hgnc:2550
      label: CELF2
  description: Heterozygous CELF2 variants that disrupt nuclear localisation. CELF2 encodes a nucleocytoplasmic
    shuttling RNA-binding protein with several roles in RNA processing and in development of the central
    nervous system and heart, so the lesion is post-transcriptional rather than one of channel conduction.
    Four of five individuals had DEE and one had intellectual disability with autistic features. All variants
    except a canonical splice site change clustered within twenty residues of the C-terminus, and mutant
    CELF2 protein was mislocalised outside the nucleus in transfected cells.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33131106
    reference_title: De novo variants in CELF2 that disrupt the nuclear localization signal cause developmental
      and epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: 'We report heterozygous CELF2 (NM_006561.3) variants in five unrelated individuals: Individuals
      1-4 exhibited developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) and Individual 5 had intellectual
      disability and autistic features.'
    explanation: Establishes the DEE97 clinical entity and heterozygous CELF2 variants as its lesion.
  - reference: PMID:33131106
    reference_title: De novo variants in CELF2 that disrupt the nuclear localization signal cause developmental
      and epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: We demonstrated the extranuclear mislocalization of mutant CELF2 protein in cells transfected
      with mutant CELF2 complementary DNA plasmids.
    explanation: Sources the mislocalisation mechanism stated in this row description.
- name: DEE98
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 98 (ATP1A2)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 98
    term:
      id: MONDO:0030472
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 98
  genes:
  - preferred_term: ATP1A2
    term:
      id: hgnc:800
      label: ATP1A2
  description: Heterozygous ATP1A2 variants at the severe end of the Na+/K+-ATPase alpha-subunit spectrum.
    The same gene is associated with familial hemiplegic migraine and alternating hemiplegia of childhood,
    which dismech curates in the Familial_Hemiplegic_Migraine entry; this subtype is instead the profound
    phenotype, featuring polymicrogyria or progressive brain atrophy with epilepsy, which caused early
    lethality in seven of 22 patients in the cited cohort. ATP1A2 accounted for six of those 22 patients,
    the remainder carrying ATP1A3 variants. Transfected-cell assays showed severely impaired pump
    activity.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33880529
    reference_title: ATP1A2- and ATP1A3-associated early profound epileptic encephalopathy and polymicrogyria.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We investigated the genetic causes of developmental and epileptic encephalopathies variably
      associated with malformations of cortical development in a large cohort and identified 22 patients
      with de novo or inherited heterozygous ATP1A2/A3 mutations.
    explanation: Establishes heterozygous ATP1A2 variants as a cause of DEE with cortical malformation.
  - reference: PMID:33880529
    reference_title: ATP1A2- and ATP1A3-associated early profound epileptic encephalopathy and polymicrogyria.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Twenty-two patients harboured 19 distinct heterozygous mutations of ATP1A2 (six patients,
      five mutations) and ATP1A3 (16 patients, 14 mutations, including a mosaic individual).
    explanation: Source for the ATP1A2 share of the cited cohort recorded here.
  - reference: PMID:33880529
    reference_title: ATP1A2- and ATP1A3-associated early profound epileptic encephalopathy and polymicrogyria.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Constitutional heterozygous mutations of ATP1A2 and ATP1A3, encoding for two distinct
      isoforms of the Na+/K+-ATPase (NKA) alpha-subunit, have been associated with familial hemiplegic
      migraine (ATP1A2), alternating hemiplegia of childhood (ATP1A2/A3), rapid-onset dystonia-parkinsonism,
      cerebellar ataxia-areflexia-progressive optic atrophy, and relapsing encephalopathy with cerebellar
      ataxia (all ATP1A3).
    explanation: Source for the other ATP1A2 phenotypes this subtype is distinguished from, and for
      the Na+/K+-ATPase alpha-subunit identity. Recorded as BACKGROUND because the citing study established
      the DEE phenotype rather than these earlier associations.
  - reference: PMID:33880529
    reference_title: ATP1A2- and ATP1A3-associated early profound epileptic encephalopathy and polymicrogyria.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: A distinctive, 'profound' phenotype, featuring polymicrogyria or progressive brain atrophy
      and epilepsy, resulted in early lethality in seven patients (32%).
    explanation: Source for the profound phenotype and the early-lethality figure recorded here.
- name: DEE100
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 100 (FBXO28)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 100
    term:
      id: MONDO:0030695
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 100
  genes:
  - preferred_term: FBXO28
    term:
      id: hgnc:29046
      label: FBXO28
  description: Heterozygous FBXO28 variants - missense, nonsense and frameshift - in one of the two
    genes in the 1q41-q42 microdeletion interval already implicated in monogenic disease. Across the
    ten cases assembled in the cited report all had epilepsy and nine of ten had DEE, including infantile
    spasms and a progressive myoclonic epilepsy. The report distinguishes FBXO28 encephalopathy from
    both 1q41-q42 deletion syndrome and WDR26 encephalopathy by more severe intellectual impairment,
    drug-resistant epilepsy and hyperkinetic movement disorders.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33280099
    reference_title: FBXO28 causes developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with profound intellectual
      disability.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We describe nine new patients with FBXO28 pathogenic variants (four missense, including
      one recurrent, three nonsense, and one frameshift) and analyze all 10 known cases to delineate
      the phenotypic spectrum. All patients had epilepsy and 9 of 10 had DEE, including infantile
      spasms (3) and a progressive myoclonic epilepsy (1).
    explanation: Establishes FBXO28 as causal and quantifies the DEE fraction of the reported cohort.
  - reference: PMID:33280099
    reference_title: FBXO28 causes developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with profound intellectual
      disability.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We distinguish FBXO28 encephalopathy from both of these disorders with more severe intellectual
      impairment, drug-resistant epilepsy, and hyperkinetic movement disorders.
    explanation: Supports separating this subtype from the overlapping 1q41-q42 deletion and WDR26
      phenotypes.
  - reference: PMID:33280099
    reference_title: FBXO28 causes developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with profound intellectual
      disability.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Two genes in the 1q41-q42 microdeletion, WDR26 and FBXO28, have been implicated in monogenic
      disease.
    explanation: Source for FBXO28 lying in the 1q41-q42 microdeletion interval. Recorded as BACKGROUND
      because the citing study set out to test the FBXO28-DEE hypothesis rather than to establish
      the interval.
- name: DEE102
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 102 (SLC38A3)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 102
    term:
      id: MONDO:0030881
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 102
  genes:
  - preferred_term: SLC38A3
    term:
      id: hgnc:18044
      label: SLC38A3
  description: 'Biallelic SLC38A3 variants. The gene encodes SNAT3, a sodium-coupled neutral amino
    acid transporter carrying asparagine, histidine and glutamine, the last being the precursor of
    both GABA and glutamate. Ten individuals from seven unrelated families in six countries were reported:
    global developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia and absent speech were common,
    with microcephaly, epilepsy and visual impairment in the majority, and epilepsy drug-resistant

  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34605855
    reference_title: Biallelic variants in SLC38A3 encoding a glutamine transporter cause epileptic
