    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Exome sequencing and family-based rare variant analyses on a cohort with neurodevelopmental
      disorders identified two siblings with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy and a shared
      deleterious homozygous splicing variant in SLC38A3.
    explanation: Establishes the founding biallelic SLC38A3 observation in DEE.
  - reference: PMID:34605855
    reference_title: Biallelic variants in SLC38A3 encoding a glutamine transporter cause epileptic
      encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Our data support the contention that SLC38A3 is a novel disease gene for developmental
      and epileptic encephalopathy and illuminate the likely pathophysiology of the disease as perturbations
      in glutamine homeostasis.
    explanation: States the gene-disease relationship and the glutamine-homeostasis mechanism.
  - reference: PMID:34605855
    reference_title: Biallelic variants in SLC38A3 encoding a glutamine transporter cause epileptic
      encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: The gene encodes SNAT3, a sodium-coupled neutral amino acid transporter and a principal
      transporter of the amino acids asparagine, histidine, and glutamine, the latter being the precursor
      for the neurotransmitters GABA and glutamate.
    explanation: Source for the SNAT3 transport function and for glutamine being the precursor of
      both GABA and glutamate. Recorded as BACKGROUND because the gene's transport function was established

  - reference: PMID:34605855
    reference_title: Biallelic variants in SLC38A3 encoding a glutamine transporter cause epileptic
      encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Ten individuals from seven unrelated families from six different countries with deleterious
      biallelic variants in SLC38A3 were identified. Global developmental delay, intellectual disability,

- name: DEE103
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 103 (KCNC2)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 103
    term:
      id: MONDO:0030957
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 103
  genes:
  - preferred_term: KCNC2
    term:
      id: hgnc:6234
      label: KCNC2
  description: 'De novo KCNC2 variants. KCNC2 encodes Kv3.2, a Shaw-related voltage-gated potassium channel
    subunit that supports sustained high-frequency firing. The defining series of eighteen patients spans
    genetic generalised epilepsy, focal epilepsy, myoclonic-atonic epilepsy and DEE, and the functional
    direction tracks severity: gain of function in three severely affected DEE cases and loss of function
    in one milder generalised-epilepsy case. Eight drug-responsive patients became seizure free on valproic
    acid alone or in combination, including severe DEE cases.'
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:35314505
    reference_title: Spectrum of Phenotypic, Genetic, and Functional Characteristics in Patients With
      Epilepsy With KCNC2 Pathogenic Variants.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We identified novel KCNC2 variants in 18 patients with various forms of epilepsy, including
      genetic generalized epilepsy (GGE), developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) including early-onset
      absence epilepsy, focal epilepsy, and myoclonic-atonic epilepsy.
    explanation: Establishes the KCNC2 phenotypic spectrum, of which DEE103 is the severe pole.
  - reference: PMID:35314505
    reference_title: Spectrum of Phenotypic, Genetic, and Functional Characteristics in Patients With
      Epilepsy With KCNC2 Pathogenic Variants.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: Functional analysis of 4 variants demonstrated gain of function in 3 severely affected DEE
      cases and loss of function in 1 case with a milder phenotype (GGE) as the underlying pathomechanisms.
    explanation: Sources the direction-of-effect correlation with severity stated in this row description.
  - reference: PMID:35314505
    reference_title: Spectrum of Phenotypic, Genetic, and Functional Characteristics in Patients With
      Epilepsy With KCNC2 Pathogenic Variants.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Eight drug-responsive patients became seizure-free using valproic acid as monotherapy or
      in combination, including severe DEE cases.
    explanation: Sources the valproate response stated in this row description.
- name: DEE104
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 104 (ATP6V0A1)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 104
    term:
      id: MONDO:0031021
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 104
  genes:
  - preferred_term: ATP6V0A1
    term:
      id: hgnc:865
      label: ATP6V0A1
  description: 'ATP6V0A1 encodes the brain-enriched a1 isoform of the V0 domain of the vacuolar H+-ATPase.
    The cited cohort splits by inheritance: five individuals with biallelic variants had early-onset
    progressive myoclonus epilepsy with ataxia, while twelve with de novo missense variants had severe

  - reference: PMID:34909687
    reference_title: Variants in ATP6V0A1 cause progressive myoclonus epilepsy and developmental and
      epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL

      of early-onset progressive myoclonus epilepsy with ataxia, while 12 individuals carried de novo
      missense variants and showed severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
    explanation: Establishes the de novo missense DEE phenotype and its separation from the biallelic
      progressive myoclonus epilepsy phenotype.
  - reference: PMID:34909687
    reference_title: Variants in ATP6V0A1 cause progressive myoclonus epilepsy and developmental and
      epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Variants in ATP6V0A1, the brain-enriched isoform in the V0 domain, have been recently
      associated with developmental delay and epilepsy in four individuals.
    explanation: Records the prior reports that established the gene-disease relationship.
  - reference: PMID:34909687
    reference_title: Variants in ATP6V0A1 cause progressive myoclonus epilepsy and developmental and
      epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: The R740Q mutation, which alone accounts for almost 50% of the mutations identified among
      our cases, leads to failure of lysosomal hydrolysis by directly impairing acidification of the
      endolysosomal compartment, causing autophagic dysfunction
    explanation: Source for the recurrent R740Q change, its share of the reported mutations, and the

- name: DEE105
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 105 with hypopituitarism (HID1)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 105 with hypopituitarism
    term:

      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 105 with hypopituitarism
  genes:
  - preferred_term: HID1
    term:
      id: hgnc:15736
      label: HID1
  description: Biallelic HID1 variants. HID1 acts in the trans-Golgi network, where precursors of peptide
    hormones are processed, which is why this subtype pairs an epileptic encephalopathy with central
    pituitary insufficiency. Seven individuals from six unrelated families

    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Bi-allelic variants in the gene HID1 domain-containing protein 1 (HID1) were identified in
      all patients.
    explanation: Establishes biallelic HID1 variants as the lesion defining this subtype.
  - reference: PMID:33999436
    reference_title: Mutations in HID1 Cause Syndromic Infantile Encephalopathy and Hypopituitarism.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We aimed to clarify the genetic cause in a group of patients characterized by hypopituitarism
      in combination with brain atrophy, thin corpus callosum, severe developmental delay, visual impairment,
      and epilepsy.
    explanation: Sources the combined endocrine and neurological phenotype that distinguishes DEE105.
  - reference: PMID:33999436
    reference_title: Mutations in HID1 Cause Syndromic Infantile Encephalopathy and Hypopituitarism.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Postmortem examination confirmed cerebral atrophy with enlarged lateral ventricles. Markedly
      reduced expression of pituitary hormones was found in pituitary gland tissue.
    explanation: Sources the neuropathological and pituitary findings stated in this row description.
- name: DEE106
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 106 (UFSP2)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 106
    term:
      id: MONDO:0031052
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 106
  genes:
  - preferred_term: UFSP2
    term:
      id: hgnc:25640
      label: UFSP2
  description: Homozygosity for the UFSP2 p.V115E variant in eight children from four South Asian
    families with neurodevelopmental delay and epilepsy. UFSP2 encodes UFM1-specific peptidase 2,
    which acts in the UFMylation pathway of protein modification; patient fibroblasts showed reduced

    reference_title: A pathogenic UFSP2 variant in an autosomal recessive form of pediatric neurodevelopmental
      anomalies and epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Homozygosity for the variant occurred in eight children from four South Asian families
      with neurodevelopmental delay and epilepsy.
    explanation: Establishes the biallelic UFSP2 lesion and the neurodevelopmental-delay-with-epilepsy
      phenotype of this subtype.
  - reference: PMID:33473208
    reference_title: A pathogenic UFSP2 variant in an autosomal recessive form of pediatric neurodevelopmental
      anomalies and epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Different UFSP2 variants cause markedly different diseases, with homozygosity for V115E
      causing a severe syndrome of neurodevelopmental disability and epilepsy.
    explanation: Supports separating this recessive neurodevelopmental subtype from the dominant UFSP2
      skeletal dysplasias.
  - reference: PMID:33473208
    reference_title: A pathogenic UFSP2 variant in an autosomal recessive form of pediatric neurodevelopmental
      anomalies and epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: Immunoblotting in patient-derived fibroblasts revealed reduced UFSP2 abundance and increased
      abundance of UFMylated targets, indicating the variant may impair de-UFMylation rather than
      UFMylation.
    explanation: Source for the impaired de-UFMylation mechanism recorded here, measured in patient

  - reference: PMID:33473208
    reference_title: A pathogenic UFSP2 variant in an autosomal recessive form of pediatric neurodevelopmental
      anomalies and epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: COMPUTATIONAL

- name: DEE107
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 107 (NAPB)
  classification: molecular

    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 107

      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 107
  genes:
  - preferred_term: NAPB
    term:
      id: hgnc:15751
      label: NAPB
  description: A homozygous nonsense NAPB variant. NAPB encodes the beta attachment protein of N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive
    factor and acts in SNARE complex dissociation and recycling during synaptic vesicle docking, so this
    subtype and DEE96 are lesions at two successive steps of the same machinery. The index patient was
    a girl of Irish Traveller descent with consanguineous parents, with multifocal seizures and profound
    global developmental delay. Napb knockout mice were already known to develop recurrent postnatal seizures
    without structural brain change.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:26235277
    reference_title: NAPB - a novel SNARE-associated protein for early-onset epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Variant prioritization identified a homozygous nonsense variant in the N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive
      factor attachment protein, beta (NAPB) gene resulting in a premature stop codon and 46% loss of
      the protein.
    explanation: Establishes the homozygous NAPB lesion defining this subtype and the extent of protein
      loss.
  - reference: PMID:26235277
    reference_title: NAPB - a novel SNARE-associated protein for early-onset epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Here, we report a 6-year-old girl with unexplained EOEE characterized by multifocal seizures
      and profound global developmental delay.
    explanation: Sources the clinical presentation of the index case.
  - reference: PMID:26235277
    reference_title: NAPB - a novel SNARE-associated protein for early-onset epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: Knockout mouse models of the murine ortholog Napb have been previously reported. These mice
      develop recurrent post-natal epileptic seizures in the absence of structural brain changes.
    explanation: Model-organism support for NAPB loss causing seizures, restated by the citing paper from
      earlier work.
- name: DEE108
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 108 (MAST3)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 108
    term:
      id: MONDO:0859314
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 108
  genes:
  - preferred_term: MAST3
    term:
      id: hgnc:19036
      label: MAST3
  description: De novo MAST3 missense variants in the serine-threonine kinase domain. MAST3 is one of
    the microtubule-associated serine-threonine kinases, expressed in excitatory cortical neurons late
    in prenatal development and postnatally. All eleven individuals of the defining series had DEE, eight
    with normal development before seizure onset under two years of age, and fever-triggered and drug-resistant
    seizures in nine each. Transfected cells showed generally lower MAST3 expression with increased phosphorylation
    of its target ARPP-16, which the authors suggest may confer gain of function.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34185323
    reference_title: Pathogenic MAST3 Variants in the STK Domain Are Associated with Epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We identify de novo missense variants in the STK domain in 11 individuals, including 2 recurrent
      variants p.G510S (n = 5) and p.G515S (n = 3).
    explanation: Establishes the de novo MAST3 kinase-domain variants that define this subtype.
  - reference: PMID:34185323
    reference_title: Pathogenic MAST3 Variants in the STK Domain Are Associated with Epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: All 11 individuals had developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, with 8 having normal development
      prior to seizure onset at <2 years of age.
    explanation: Sources the DEE phenotype and the normal pre-seizure development stated in this row description.
  - reference: PMID:34185323
    reference_title: Pathogenic MAST3 Variants in the STK Domain Are Associated with Epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: All patients developed multiple seizure types, 9 of 11 patients had seizures triggered by
      fever and 9 of 11 patients had drug-resistant seizures.
    explanation: Sources the fever trigger and drug resistance counts stated in this row description.
- name: DEE109
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 109 (FZR1)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 109
    term:
      id: MONDO:0859325
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 109
  genes:
  - preferred_term: FZR1
    term:
      id: hgnc:24824
      label: FZR1
  description: De novo loss-of-function FZR1 variants. FZR1 encodes the Cdh1 subunit of the anaphase-promoting
    complex, with roles both in the cell cycle and in post-mitotic neurons, so the lesion is in cell-cycle
    regulation rather than in a channel or synaptic protein. The three individuals found among 250 unrelated
    DEE patients all had childhood-onset generalised epilepsy, intellectual disability, mild ataxia and
    normal head circumference, and two were diagnosed with the myoclonic atonic epilepsy subtype of DEE.
    Drosophila assays using three mutant alleles of the homologue fzr supported the variants being loss
    of function.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34788397
    reference_title: De novo FZR1 loss-of-function variants cause developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: In this study, evaluation of 250 unrelated patients with developmental and epileptic encephalopathies
      and a connection on GeneMatcher led to the identification of three de novo missense variants in
      FZR1.
    explanation: Establishes the de novo FZR1 variants that define this subtype and how they were ascertained.
  - reference: PMID:34788397
    reference_title: De novo FZR1 loss-of-function variants cause developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: All three individuals carrying de novo variants in FZR1 had childhood-onset generalized epilepsy,
      intellectual disability, mild ataxia and normal head circumference.
    explanation: Sources the phenotype stated in this row description.
  - reference: PMID:34788397
    reference_title: De novo FZR1 loss-of-function variants cause developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: Further, we provide functional evidence that the missense variants are loss-of-function alleles
      using Drosophila neurodevelopment assays.
    explanation: Sources the loss-of-function reading of the FZR1 variants.
- name: DEE110
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 110 (CACNA2D1)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 110

      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 110
  genes:
  - preferred_term: CACNA2D1
    term:
      id: hgnc:1399
      label: CACNA2D1
  description: Biallelic loss-of-function CACNA2D1 variants in two unrelated individuals. CACNA2D1
    encodes the α2δ-1 auxiliary subunit of CaV1 and CaV2 voltage-gated calcium channels. Functional
    studies of the missense allele carried by one of the two showed that the amino-acid change severely
    impairs α2δ-1's function as a calcium channel subunit.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:35293990
    reference_title: Biallelic CACNA2D1 loss-of-function variants cause early-onset developmental

    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Here we report biallelic variants in CACNA2D1, encoding the α2δ-1 protein, in two unrelated

    explanation: Establishes biallelic CACNA2D1 variants as the lesion defining this subtype.
  - reference: PMID:35293990
    reference_title: Biallelic CACNA2D1 loss-of-function variants cause early-onset developmental
      epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Thus, biallelic loss-of-function variants in CACNA2D1 underlie the severe neurodevelopmental
      disorder in these two patients.
    explanation: States the loss-of-function mechanism and the severity of the resulting neurodevelopmental
      disorder.
  - reference: PMID:35293990
    reference_title: Biallelic CACNA2D1 loss-of-function variants cause early-onset developmental
      epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: Our functional studies show that this amino-acid change severely impairs the function
      of α2δ-1 as a calcium channel subunit
    explanation: Source for the functional impairment of the auxiliary subunit recorded here.
- name: DEE111
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 111 (DEPDC5, biallelic)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 111
    term:
      id: MONDO:0957780
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 111
  genes:
  - preferred_term: DEPDC5
    term:
      id: hgnc:18423
      label: DEPDC5
  description: 'Germline biallelic missense DEPDC5 variants. DEPDC5 encodes an inhibitory component of
    the mTOR pathway, and the usual germline lesion is a single inactivating heterozygous variant, which
    dismech curates as the separate DEPDC5-Related_Epilepsy entry. This subtype is the biallelic germline
    phenotype, which is a different entity: extensive bilateral polymicrogyria, congenital macrocephaly
    and early-onset refractory epilepsy, rather than a focal lesion produced by a brain-somatic second
    hit. Six of the children were of Irish Traveller origin sharing p.Thr337Arg, and two Tunisian plus
    one Lebanese child shared p.Arg806Cys; five of nine died in infancy or childhood.'
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:36067010
    reference_title: Germline homozygous missense DEPDC5 variants cause severe refractory early-onset
      epilepsy, macrocephaly and bilateral polymicrogyria.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We describe a novel phenotype caused by germline biallelic missense variants in DEPDC5.
    explanation: Establishes the biallelic germline DEPDC5 entity that this subtype term names, as distinct
      from heterozygous DEPDC5-related focal epilepsy.
  - reference: PMID:36067010
    reference_title: Germline homozygous missense DEPDC5 variants cause severe refractory early-onset
      epilepsy, macrocephaly and bilateral polymicrogyria.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Consistent phenotypic features included extensive bilateral polymicrogyria, congenital macrocephaly
      and early-onset refractory epilepsy, in keeping with other mTOR-opathies.
    explanation: Sources the phenotype stated in this row description, and its bilateral rather than focal
      distribution.
  - reference: PMID:36067010
    reference_title: Germline homozygous missense DEPDC5 variants cause severe refractory early-onset
      epilepsy, macrocephaly and bilateral polymicrogyria.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Skin biopsy immunohistochemistry was supportive of hyperactivation of the mTOR pathway.
    explanation: Sources the mTOR hyperactivation mechanism in affected individuals.
- name: DEE112
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 112 (KCNH5)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 112
    term:
      id: MONDO:0957812
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 112
  genes:
  - preferred_term: KCNH5
    term:
      id: hgnc:6254
      label: KCNH5
  description: 'De novo KCNH5 missense variants in or near the voltage-sensing and pore domains. KCNH5
    encodes the voltage-gated potassium channel EAG2/Kv10.2. The defining cohort of seventeen patients
    shows that the severity tracks the variant rather than the gene: the recurrent p.Arg333His gave a
    self-limited drug-responsive epilepsy with normal intellect, while the recurrent p.Arg327His gave
    infantile-onset DEE, and two pore-domain variants gave a neonatal movement disorder with early-infantile
    DEE, profound disability and childhood death.'
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:36307226
    reference_title: Neurodevelopmental and Epilepsy Phenotypes in Individuals With Missense Variants
      in the Voltage-Sensing and Pore Domains of KCNH5.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We report a cohort of 17 patients, including 9 with a recurrent de novo missense variant
      p.Arg327His, 4 with a recurrent missense variant p.Arg333His, and 4 additional novel missense variants.
    explanation: Establishes the KCNH5 variant series behind this subtype.
  - reference: PMID:36307226
    reference_title: Neurodevelopmental and Epilepsy Phenotypes in Individuals With Missense Variants
      in the Voltage-Sensing and Pore Domains of KCNH5.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Individuals with the recurrent p.Arg333His variant had a self-limited drug-responsive focal
      or generalized epilepsy and normal intellect, whereas the recurrent p.Arg327His variant was associated
      with infantile-onset DEE.
    explanation: Sources the variant-dependent split between self-limited epilepsy and DEE stated in this
      row description.
- name: DEE113
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 113 (SV2A)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 113
    term:
      id: MONDO:0958330
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 113
  genes:
  - preferred_term: SV2A
    term:
      id: hgnc:20566
      label: SV2A
  description: 'SV2A encodes synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A, the binding site of levetiracetam.
    The reported lesion is a homozygous R383Q missense change in a multiply consanguineous family:
    the proband had intractable epilepsy, involuntary movements, microcephaly and developmental and
    growth retardation, and an earlier-born brother had a similar course and died at 7 months of age.
    Levetiracetam was not effective in the proband. The evidence base for this subtype is thin - a
    single family, with no independent replication found in a PubMed search on 2026-09-25 using the
    queries ''SV2A biallelic variants developmental and epileptic encephalopathy'' (no hits), ''SV2A
    gene variants patients epilepsy developmental delay cohort'' (no hits) and ''synaptic vesicle
    glycoprotein 2A SV2A homozygous variant patients'' (this report only).'
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:26002053
    reference_title: Homozygous Mutation in Synaptic Vesicle Glycoprotein 2A Gene Results in Intractable
      Epilepsy, Involuntary Movements, Microcephaly, and Developmental and Growth Retardation.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Exome sequencing identified a homozygous arginine to glutamine mutation in amino acid
      position 383 (R383Q) in exon 5 of the SV2A gene.
    explanation: Establishes the single reported biallelic SV2A lesion defining this subtype.
  - reference: PMID:26002053
    reference_title: Homozygous Mutation in Synaptic Vesicle Glycoprotein 2A Gene Results in Intractable
      Epilepsy, Involuntary Movements, Microcephaly, and Developmental and Growth Retardation.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Our report provides the elusive evidence that an SV2A mutation can be a cause of epilepsy
      in humans.
    explanation: States the gene-disease claim, and its wording marks how new and singular the observation
      was.
  - reference: PMID:26002053
    reference_title: Homozygous Mutation in Synaptic Vesicle Glycoprotein 2A Gene Results in Intractable
      Epilepsy, Involuntary Movements, Microcephaly, and Developmental and Growth Retardation.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Both parents were multiply consanguineous and an earlier-born brother of the proband
      had a similar course and died at 7 months of age.
    explanation: Source for the consanguinity and the affected sibling, the whole of the reported
      family evidence for this subtype.
  - reference: PMID:26002053
    reference_title: Homozygous Mutation in Synaptic Vesicle Glycoprotein 2A Gene Results in Intractable
      Epilepsy, Involuntary Movements, Microcephaly, and Developmental and Growth Retardation.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We investigated a patient with intractable epilepsy, involuntary movements, microcephaly,
      and developmental and growth retardation.
    explanation: Source for the proband's phenotype recorded here.
- name: DEE114
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 114 (SLC32A1)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 114
    term:
      id: MONDO:0958331
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 114
  genes:
  - preferred_term: SLC32A1
    term:
      id: hgnc:11018
      label: SLC32A1
  description: 'De novo missense SLC32A1 variants. SLC32A1 encodes the vesicular GABA transporter, which
    loads GABA into synaptic vesicles, so the lesion is presynaptic and inhibitory. Inherited missense
    variants in the same gene had already been linked to genetic epilepsy with febrile seizures plus,
    and this report establishes that de novo missense variants instead cause a DEE. Two mechanisms were
    demonstrated in a murine neuronal culture model: three variants lining the putative GABA transport
    pathway reduced quantal size, consistent with impaired vesicle filling, while an N-terminal variant
    left quantal size intact but raised presynaptic release probability.'
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:36073542
    reference_title: De Novo Missense Variants in SLC32A1 Cause a Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy
      Due to Impaired GABAergic Neurotransmission.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Using exome sequencing, we identified four individuals with a developmental and epileptic
      encephalopathy and de novo missense variants in SLC32A1.
    explanation: Establishes the DEE114 clinical entity and de novo SLC32A1 variants as its lesion.
  - reference: PMID:36073542
    reference_title: De Novo Missense Variants in SLC32A1 Cause a Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy
      Due to Impaired GABAergic Neurotransmission.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: The main phenotype comprises moderate-to-severe intellectual disability, infantile-onset
      epilepsy within the first 18 months of life, and a choreiform, dystonic, or dyskinetic movement
      disorder.
    explanation: Sources the phenotype stated in this row description, including the movement disorder.
  - reference: PMID:36073542
    reference_title: De Novo Missense Variants in SLC32A1 Cause a Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy
      Due to Impaired GABAergic Neurotransmission.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: In silico modeling and functional analyses reveal that three of these variants, which are
      located in helices that line the putative GABA transport pathway, result in reduced quantal size,
      consistent with impaired filling of synaptic vesicles with GABA.
    explanation: Sources the vesicle-filling mechanism, measured in a murine neuronal cell culture model.
- name: DEE115
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 115 (SNF8)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 115

      id: MONDO:0968946
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 115
  genes:
  - preferred_term: SNF8
    term:
      id: hgnc:17028
      label: SNF8
  description: Biallelic SNF8 variants, the severe pole of the SNF8 disease spectrum. SNF8 encodes a subunit
    of ESCRT-II, one of the three complexes of the endosomal sorting machinery required for membrane remodelling
    and autophagy. The milder pole of the same spectrum, with intellectual disability and childhood-onset

  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:38423010
    reference_title: Bi-allelic variants in SNF8 cause a disease spectrum ranging from severe developmental
      and epileptic encephalopathy to syndromic optic atrophy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: The phenotypic spectrum included four individuals with severe developmental and epileptic
      encephalopathy, massive reduction of white matter, hypo-/aplasia of the corpus callosum, neurodevelopmental
      arrest, and early death.
    explanation: Establishes the DEE115 clinical entity as the severe pole of the SNF8 spectrum.
  - reference: PMID:38423010
    reference_title: Bi-allelic variants in SNF8 cause a disease spectrum ranging from severe developmental
      and epileptic encephalopathy to syndromic optic atrophy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: 'We report nine individuals from six families presenting with a spectrum of neurodevelopmental/neurodegenerative
      features caused by bi-allelic variants in SNF8 (GenBank: NM_007241.4), encoding the ESCRT-II subunit
      SNF8.'
    explanation: Establishes biallelic SNF8 variants as the lesion and SNF8 as an ESCRT-II subunit.
  - reference: PMID:38423010
    reference_title: Bi-allelic variants in SNF8 cause a disease spectrum ranging from severe developmental
      and epileptic encephalopathy to syndromic optic atrophy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: All mildly affected individuals shared the same hypomorphic variant, c.304G>A (p.Val102Ile).
    explanation: Sources the allele that separates the mild pole, curated elsewhere, from this severe
      pole.
- name: DEE118
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 118 (TMEM63B)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 118
    term:
      id: MONDO:0979238
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 118
  mappings:
    mondo_mappings:
    - term:
        id: MONDO:0800503
        label: TMEM63B-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with anemia
      mapping_predicate: skos:exactMatch
      mapping_source: MONDO
      mapping_justification: 'MONDO carries two classes for one disease. MONDO:0800503 and MONDO:0979238
        are both direct children of MONDO:0100062, both assert RO:0004003 hgnc:17735 TMEM63B, and both
        trace to the same founding report: the OMIM summary for OMIM:621250, which MONDO:0979238 xrefs,
        attributes the phenotype to Vetro et al. 2023 (PMID:37421948), and the haematological abnormality
        that MONDO:0800503 is named after is the feature that report describes in 12 of 17 individuals.
        The two classes differ only in provenance, MONDO:0800503 carrying GARD:0027306 and MONDO:0979238
        carrying OMIM:621250 and GARD:0028112, and neither definition refers to the other or gives a reason
        for a split.'
  genes:
  - preferred_term: TMEM63B
    term:
      id: hgnc:17735
      label: TMEM63B
  description: 'Heterozygous, almost always de novo, missense or in-frame TMEM63B variants affecting conserved
    transmembrane residues. TMEM63B encodes a stretch-activated ion channel, and the mutated channels
    carried an inward leak cation current even under isotonic conditions while responding poorly to a
    hypo-osmotic challenge. Two features set this subtype apart from the other channel subtypes here:
    the brain changes are progressive and neurodegenerative rather than static, and haematological abnormalities
    such as macrocytosis and haemolysis occurred in twelve of seventeen individuals, some needing transfusion.
    The recurrent p.Val44Met accounted for seven of the seventeen.'
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:37421948
    reference_title: Stretch-activated ion channel TMEM63B associates with developmental and epileptic
      encephalopathies and progressive neurodegeneration.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Here, we describe 17 unrelated individuals with severe early-onset developmental and epileptic
      encephalopathy (DEE), intellectual disability, and severe motor and cortical visual impairment associated
      with progressive neurodegenerative brain changes carrying ten distinct heterozygous variants of
      TMEM63B, encoding for a highly conserved stretch-activated ion channel.
    explanation: Establishes the clinical entity, the heterozygous TMEM63B lesion, and the progressive
      neurodegenerative course.
  - reference: PMID:37421948
    reference_title: Stretch-activated ion channel TMEM63B associates with developmental and epileptic
      encephalopathies and progressive neurodegeneration.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: In 12 individuals, hematological abnormalities co-occurred, such as macrocytosis and hemolysis,
      requiring blood transfusions in some.
    explanation: Sources the haematological involvement, which is the feature the duplicate MONDO class
      named in this row mappings block is named after.
  - reference: PMID:37421948
    reference_title: Stretch-activated ion channel TMEM63B associates with developmental and epileptic
      encephalopathies and progressive neurodegeneration.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: we modeled six variants (p.Val44Met, p.Arg433His, p.Thr481Asn, p.Gly580Ser, p.Arg660Thr,
      and p.Phe697Leu), each affecting a distinct transmembrane domain of the channel, in transfected
      Neuro2a cells and demonstrated inward leak cation currents across the mutated channel even in isotonic
      conditions
    explanation: Sources the leak-current mechanism stated in this row description.

      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 119
  genes:
  - preferred_term: RNU2-2
    term:
      id: hgnc:10152
      label: RNU2-2P
  description: Recurrent de novo single-nucleotide mutations at positions 4 and 35 of RNU2-2, a 191-bp
    gene encoding the U2-2 small nuclear RNA of the major spliceosome. Twenty-five cases were assembled
    in the founding report, which estimates the disorder's prevalence at about 20% that of the related
    RNU4-2 syndrome. The phenotype is intellectual disability, autistic behaviour, microcephaly, hypotonia,
    epilepsy and hyperventilation, with a severe and complex seizure phenotype in all cases. Notably,
    mutant U2-2 was expressed in patient blood without detectable missplicing, so the mechanism downstream
    of the snRNA lesion is not yet established. This is the only non-protein-coding causal gene among
    the subtypes recorded here.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40210679
    reference_title: Mutations in the small nuclear RNA gene RNU2-2 cause a severe neurodevelopmental
      disorder with prominent epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: By genetic association, we identified recurrent de novo single-nucleotide mutations at
      nucleotide positions 4 and 35 of RNU2-2 in nine cases.
    explanation: Establishes the recurrent de novo RNU2-2 lesion defining this subtype.
  - reference: PMID:40210679
    reference_title: Mutations in the small nuclear RNA gene RNU2-2 cause a severe neurodevelopmental
      disorder with prominent epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: The disorder is characterized by intellectual disability, autistic behavior, microcephaly,
      hypotonia, epilepsy and hyperventilation. All cases display a severe and complex seizure phenotype.
    explanation: Source for the phenotype and the uniformly severe seizure picture recorded here.
  - reference: PMID:40210679
    reference_title: Mutations in the small nuclear RNA gene RNU2-2 cause a severe neurodevelopmental
      disorder with prominent epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We replicated this finding in 16 additional cases, bringing the total to 25. We estimate
      that RNU2-2 syndrome has a prevalence of ~20% that of RNU4-2 syndrome.
    explanation: Source for the total case count and the prevalence estimate relative to RNU4-2 syndrome.
  - reference: PMID:40210679
    reference_title: Mutations in the small nuclear RNA gene RNU2-2 cause a severe neurodevelopmental
      disorder with prominent epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Despite mutant U2-2 being expressed in patient blood samples, we found no evidence of
      missplicing.
    explanation: Source for the negative missplicing result, which is why the mechanism downstream
      of the snRNA lesion is recorded as unestablished.
- name: DEE120
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 120 (BAIAP2)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 120
    term:
      id: MONDO:0980948
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 120
  genes:
  - preferred_term: BAIAP2
    term:
      id: hgnc:947
      label: BAIAP2
  description: De novo missense BAIAP2 variants in six patients. BAIAP2 acts in dendritic spine morphogenesis
    and excitatory synapse formation, and the reported variants cluster in the multiple phosphorylation
    site region that maintains the protein's autoinhibited conformation through 14-3-3 binding. All
    six patients had severe infantile or early childhood onset epilepsy, refractory in four, with
    language and motor delay and varying degrees of intellectual disability. Neurons expressing the
    variants were more excitable through enhanced excitatory synaptogenesis, which the authors read
    as gain of function.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:41133935
    reference_title: De novo missense variants in BAIAP2 are associated with developmental and epileptic
      encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Using whole exome/genome sequencing, we identified de novo missense variants in BAIAP2
      in six patients with DEEs.
    explanation: Establishes de novo BAIAP2 missense variants as the lesion defining this subtype.
  - reference: PMID:41133935
    reference_title: De novo missense variants in BAIAP2 are associated with developmental and epileptic
      encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Brain-specific angiogenesis inhibitor 1-associated protein 2 (BAIAP2) plays a crucial
      role in dendritic spine morphogenesis and excitatory synapse formation.
    explanation: States the synaptic function that places this lesion in the synaptic arm of the mechanism.
  - reference: PMID:41133935
    reference_title: De novo missense variants in BAIAP2 are associated with developmental and epileptic
      encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: All six patients exhibited severe infantile or early childhood onset epilepsy, with refractory
      seizures in four individuals.
    explanation: Source for the seizure onset and refractoriness recorded here.
  - reference: PMID:41133935
    reference_title: De novo missense variants in BAIAP2 are associated with developmental and epileptic
      encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: Electrophysiological recordings revealed that neurons expressing BAIAP2 variants exhibited
      increased excitability, due to enhanced excitatory synaptogenesis.
    explanation: Source for the gain-of-function effect on excitability, measured in cultured neurons.
  - reference: PMID:41133935
    reference_title: De novo missense variants in BAIAP2 are associated with developmental and epileptic
      encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: The missense variants were clustered within the multiple phosphorylation site region
      that is critical for the autoinhibited conformation of BAIAP2 through 14-3-3 binding.
    explanation: Source for the variant clustering and the autoinhibition mechanism recorded here.
- name: DEE121
  display_name: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 121 (LGI1)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 121
    term:
      id: MONDO:0980966
      label: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 121
  genes:
  - preferred_term: LGI1
    term:
      id: hgnc:6572
      label: LGI1
  description: Biallelic LGI1 variants - the recessive counterpart of the dominant LGI1 disease, autosomal
    dominant epilepsy with auditory features, which dismech curates as the separate Autosomal_Dominant_Epilepsy_with_Auditory_Features
    entry. Six individuals from four consanguineous families had DEE with neonatal or infantile-onset
    epilepsy and global developmental delay or intellectual disability; five of the six died in infancy
    or prematurely. All variants reduced LGI1 secretion and ADAM22 binding, and residual LGI1 function
    correlated with clinical severity. LGI1 is the ligand for ADAM22, so DEE121 and the ADAM22 subtype
    DEE61 are two ends of one pathway.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40455867
    reference_title: Biallelic LGI1 and ADAM23 variants cause hippocampal epileptic encephalopathy
      via the LGI1-ADAM22/23 pathway.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Through international genetic data sharing, we identified the first ultra-rare biallelic
      LGI1 variants in six individuals from four consanguineous families. Affected individuals presented
      DEE with neonatal/infantile-onset epilepsy (n = 6/6), global developmental delay/intellectual
      disability (n = 6/6) and infant/premature death (n = 5/6).
    explanation: Establishes biallelic LGI1 variants as a cause of DEE and records the cohort and
      its mortality.
  - reference: PMID:40455867
    reference_title: Biallelic LGI1 and ADAM23 variants cause hippocampal epileptic encephalopathy
      via the LGI1-ADAM22/23 pathway.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: LGI1 is a secreted neuronal protein, functions as a ligand for ADAM22/23, and regulates
      excitatory synaptic transmission and neuronal excitability in the brain.
    explanation: States the synaptic function shared with the ADAM22 subtype DEE61.
  - reference: PMID:40455867
    reference_title: Biallelic LGI1 and ADAM23 variants cause hippocampal epileptic encephalopathy
      via the LGI1-ADAM22/23 pathway.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: Functional analyses revealed that all LGI1 variants result in reduced secretion and ADAM22-binding.
      Residual LGI1 function levels correlated with clinical severity, ranging from infantile lethality
      to intermediate phenotypes.
    explanation: Source for the reduced secretion and ADAM22 binding, and for the correlation between
      residual function and severity.
  - reference: PMID:40455867
    reference_title: Biallelic LGI1 and ADAM23 variants cause hippocampal epileptic encephalopathy
      via the LGI1-ADAM22/23 pathway.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Monoallelic pathogenic variants in LGI1 cause autosomal dominant epilepsy with auditory
      features with onset in childhood/adolescence.
    explanation: Source for the dominant LGI1 phenotype that this recessive subtype is distinguished
      from, and for the same distinction drawn on the ADAM22 subtype DEE61. Recorded as BACKGROUND
      because the citing study established the recessive phenotype, not the dominant one.
- name: MCSZ
  display_name: Microcephaly, seizures, and developmental delay (PNKP)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: microcephaly, seizures, and developmental delay
    term:
      id: MONDO:0013254
      label: microcephaly, seizures, and developmental delay
  genes:
  - preferred_term: PNKP
    term:
      id: hgnc:9154
      label: PNKP
  description: 'Biallelic PNKP variants. This is the one subtype recorded here that MONDO does not
    number in the DEE series: it is filed under both microcephaly and genetic developmental and epileptic
    encephalopathy, and carries EIEE10 only as a related synonym. The founding report mapped the locus
    to 19q13.33 and described an autosomal recessive disease of microcephaly, early-onset intractable
    seizures and developmental delay, with a splicing allele giving a milder course. PNKP encodes
    polynucleotide kinase 3''-phosphatase; unlike other human DNA repair defects, PNKP variants universally
    cause severe seizures. Allelic PNKP disorders are curated elsewhere in dismech, notably Charcot-Marie-Tooth_Disease_Type_2B2.'
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:20118933
    reference_title: Mutations in PNKP cause microcephaly, seizures and defects in DNA repair.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We describe a previously unknown autosomal recessive disease characterized by microcephaly,
      early-onset, intractable seizures and developmental delay (denoted MCSZ).
    explanation: Establishes the MCSZ entity and its autosomal recessive inheritance.
  - reference: PMID:20118933
    reference_title: Mutations in PNKP cause microcephaly, seizures and defects in DNA repair.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Unlike other DNA repair defects that affect humans, PNKP mutations universally cause
      severe seizures.
    explanation: Supports treating this DNA-repair disorder as a member of the DEE umbrella rather
      than only a microcephaly syndrome.

- name: RMFSL
  display_name: Neonatal-onset encephalopathy with rigidity and seizures (BRAT1)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: neonatal-onset encephalopathy with rigidity and seizures
    term:
      id: MONDO:0013784
      label: neonatal-onset encephalopathy with rigidity and seizures
  genes:
  - preferred_term: BRAT1
    term:
      id: hgnc:21701
      label: BRAT1
  description: 'Biallelic BRAT1 variants, also called lethal neonatal rigidity and multifocal seizure
    syndrome. BRAT1 is the BRCA1-associated ATM activator. The sibling pair in the first report cited
    here carried compound heterozygous variants, one of them affecting a conserved residue in the CIDE-N
    domain that regulates the DNA fragmentation pathway of apoptosis. BRAT1 produces two distinct phenotypes,
    and which one a genotype gives is largely predictable: in a 97-patient cohort every one of 46 genotypes
    made up of biallelic nonsense, frameshift or in-frame indel variants gave this lethal rigidity and
    multifocal-seizure phenotype, whereas genotypes including at least one missense variant gave the non-lethal
    cerebellar-atrophy phenotype in 28 of 34. Fifty-nine of the 97 had the phenotype this row names, and
    93 per cent of those died prematurely.'
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25319849
    reference_title: Compound heterozygous BRAT1 mutations cause familial Ohtahara syndrome with hypertonia
      and microcephaly.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: They had intractable seizures from neonatal period, dysmorphic features and hypertonia. Progressive
      microcephaly was also observed.
    explanation: Clinical presentation of the sibling pair reported in this paper, who carried compound
      heterozygous BRAT1 variants.
  - reference: PMID:25319849
    reference_title: Compound heterozygous BRAT1 mutations cause familial Ohtahara syndrome with hypertonia
      and microcephaly.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Homozygous frameshift BRAT1 mutations were found in patients with lethal neonatal rigidity
      and multifocal seizure syndrome (MIM# 614498).
    explanation: Identifies BRAT1 as the gene of the OMIM entity this subtype term names. The citing paper
      restates this from the earlier reports rather than establishing it.
  - reference: PMID:37344571
    reference_title: 'BRAT1-related disorders: phenotypic spectrum and phenotype-genotype correlations
      from 97 patients.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Genotype-phenotype correlations in our cohort revealed that biallelic nonsense, frameshift
      or inframe deletion/insertion variants result in the severe BRAT1-related RMFSL phenotype (46/46;
      100%). In contrast, genotypes with at least one missense were more likely associated with NEDCAS
      (28/34; 82%).
    explanation: Sources the genotype-phenotype split between this lethal phenotype and the non-lethal
      BRAT1 phenotype.
  - reference: PMID:37344571
    reference_title: 'BRAT1-related disorders: phenotypic spectrum and phenotype-genotype correlations
      from 97 patients.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Fifty-nine individuals presented with BRAT1-related RMFSL phenotype. Most of them had no
      psychomotor acquisition (100%), epilepsy (100%), microcephaly (91%), limb rigidity (93%), and died
      prematurely (93%).
    explanation: Sources the cohort share and the feature frequencies stated in this row description.
pathophysiology:
- name: Genetic Lesion in an Ion Channel or Synaptic Gene
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  description: >-
    A de novo or inherited pathogenic variant in one of a large and growing
    set of genes encoding voltage-gated ion channels (e.g. SCN1A, SCN2A,
    SCN8A, KCNQ2, KCNA2, KCNT1, CACNA1E, HCN1), presynaptic vesicle-cycle
    and neurotransmitter-release machinery (STXBP1, DNM1, SNAP25, CPLX1,
    UNC13A), postsynaptic glutamate or GABA receptors (GRIN1, GRIN2A,
    GRIN2B, GABRA1, GABRB3), or chromatin/transcriptional regulators active
    in neurodevelopment (CDKL5, FOXG1, CHD2) disrupts normal neuronal
    excitability or synaptic signaling.

    Gene-defined subtypes wired at this node in this entry, beyond the examples
    above, are CACNA2D1 (the alpha-2-delta-1 auxiliary subunit of CaV1 and CaV2
    voltage-gated calcium channels), FGF13/FHF2 (an intracellular regulator of
    voltage-gated sodium channels), SV2A (a synaptic vesicle glycoprotein and the
    binding site of levetiracetam), FRRS1L (an AMPA receptor outer-core protein),
    LGI1 together with its postsynaptic receptor ADAM22, BAIAP2 (dendritic spine
    morphogenesis and excitatory synapse formation), and ACTL6B (a subunit of the
    neuron-specific chromatin remodelling complex nBAF). Each functional
    assignment is taken from the publication cited on that subtype's own
    has_subtypes row.

    The DEE-series subtypes added under this parent extend that list with four
    further voltage-gated channel subunits (SCN3A/Nav1.3, KCNC2/Kv3.2,
    KCNH5/EAG2-Kv10.2, and the sodium-activated potassium channel KCNT2); the
    stretch-activated channel TMEM63B; four GABA receptor subunits, namely the
    GABA-A subunits GABRB2, GABRA2 and GABRA5 together with the metabotropic
    GABA-B subunit GABBR2; the vesicular GABA transporter SLC32A1; and three
    further components of the presynaptic vesicle cycle, namely the AAA ATPase
    NSF, which acts in SNARE complex assembly and disassembly, its beta
    attachment protein NAPB, and the polyphosphoinositide phosphatase SYNJ1.

  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39237642
    reference_title: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      900 genes have been identified as monogenic causes of DEEs and many cell
      components and processes
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the extreme monogenic heterogeneity of the DEE umbrella, the
      defining upstream trigger of this entry.
  - reference: PMID:35951482
    reference_title: 'Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies: from genetic heterogeneity to phenotypic continuum.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Genetic DEEs have been associated with mutations in many genes involved in
      different functions including cell migration, proliferation, and
      organization, neuronal excitability, and synapse transmission and
      plasticity.
    explanation: >-
      Enumerates the functional gene classes affected, matching the ion-channel,
      synaptic, and neurodevelopmental categories described in this node.
  downstream:
  - target: Neuronal Excitation-Inhibition Imbalance
    description: >-
      The gene-level lesion alters neuronal excitability or synaptic signalling,
      shifting the excitation-inhibition balance of the network.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:35951482
      reference_title: 'Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies: from genetic heterogeneity to phenotypic continuum.'
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        Genetic DEEs have been associated with mutations in many genes involved
        in different functions including cell migration, proliferation, and
        organization, neuronal excitability, and synapse transmission and
        plasticity.
      explanation: >-
        Connects the causal genes to neuronal excitability and synaptic
        transmission, the substrate of excitation-inhibition balance.
- name: Neuronal Excitation-Inhibition Imbalance
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  conforms_to: "epilepsy_excitation_inhibition_imbalance#Excitation-Inhibition Imbalance"
  description: >-
    Depending on the specific gene and variant, the molecular lesion produces
    either a gain- or loss-of-function shift in neuronal excitability (e.g.
    gain-of-function SCN2A/SCN8A sodium-channel variants causing neuronal
    hyperexcitability versus loss-of-function SCN1A variants preferentially
    impairing GABAergic interneuron firing), converging on a common circuit-level
    disruption of the balance between excitatory and inhibitory synaptic drive.
  cell_types:
  - preferred_term: GABAergic interneuron
    term:
      id: CL:0000617
      label: GABAergic neuron
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: GABA Signaling Pathway
    term:
      id: GO:0007214
      label: gamma-aminobutyric acid signaling pathway
    modifier: DECREASED
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39858526
    reference_title: 'Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy: Pathogenesis of Intellectual Disability Beyond Channelopathies.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Many genes mutated in DEEs encode ion channels, causing current conduction
      disruptions known as channelopathies.
    explanation: >-
      Supports the channelopathy arm in which the genetic lesion alters neuronal
      excitability, the proximate cause of excitation-inhibition imbalance.
  downstream:
  - target: Hypersynchronous Network Activity and Seizures
    description: >-
      Excitation-inhibition imbalance drives the seizure arm of the DEE
      mechanism.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:39858526
      reference_title: 'Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy: Pathogenesis of Intellectual Disability Beyond Channelopathies.'
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        Many genes mutated in DEEs encode ion channels, causing current
        conduction disruptions known as channelopathies.
      explanation: >-
        Links the channel-level conduction disruption to the epileptic output of
        the disease.
  - target: Impaired Synaptic Maturation and Neurodevelopment
    description: >-
      The same molecular lesion independently disrupts circuit maturation,
      producing the developmental arm.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:39858526
      reference_title: 'Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy: Pathogenesis of Intellectual Disability Beyond Channelopathies.'
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        These two aspects
        influence one another but can develop independently, creating diagnostic
        and therapeutic challenges.
      explanation: >-
        Supports branching the mechanism into two arms that can develop
        independently of one another.
- name: Hypersynchronous Network Activity and Seizures
  biological_scale: TISSUE
  conforms_to: "epilepsy_excitation_inhibition_imbalance#Neuronal Hyperexcitability and Hypersynchrony"
  description: >-
    Excitation-inhibition imbalance produces hypersynchronous, epileptiform
    cortical network activity, manifesting clinically as frequent,
    often multiple, drug-resistant seizure types with an abnormal
    interictal EEG background.
  cell_types:
  - preferred_term: neuron
    term:
      id: CL:0000540
      label: neuron
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: Action Potential
    term:
      id: GO:0001508
      label: action potential
    modifier: INCREASED
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40013914
    reference_title: Operational definition of developmental and epileptic encephalopathies to underpin the design of therapeutic trials.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs) are the most severe
      group of epilepsies, characterized by drug-resistant seizures and
      developmental slowing or regression.
    explanation: >-
      The ILAE operational definition identifies drug-resistant seizures as a
      defining clinical output of the DEE network mechanism.
  downstream:
  - target: Drug-Resistant Seizures
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    description: >-
      The hypersynchronous network state is what is observed clinically as the
      antiseizure-medication-refractory seizures that the ILAE operational
      definition puts at the centre of the DEE concept.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:40013914
      reference_title: Operational definition of developmental and epileptic encephalopathies to underpin the design of therapeutic trials.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs) are the most severe
        group of epilepsies, characterized by drug-resistant seizures and
        developmental slowing or regression.
      explanation: >-
        Names drug-resistant seizures as the defining clinical output of the DEE
        mechanism, which is what this edge asserts.
  - target: Status Epilepticus
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    description: >-
      Status epilepticus is the failure of a seizure to self-terminate.
      Convulsive status epilepticus was recorded in 47 per cent and
      nonconvulsive status epilepticus in 19 per cent of a 510-patient genetic
      DEE cohort.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:36750385
      reference_title: Rates of Status Epilepticus and Sudden Unexplained Death in Epilepsy in People With Genetic Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathies.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        The cohort comprised 510 individuals with a genetic DEE, in whom we
        observed CSE in 47% and NCSE in 19%.
      explanation: >-
        Quantifies status epilepticus as an outcome of the seizure mechanism in a
        cohort restricted to genetic DEE.
  - target: Abnormal EEG Background
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    description: >-
      The same hypersynchrony is recorded interictally as frequent epileptiform
      activity on an abnormal EEG background, which is the electrographic rather
      than the clinical reading of this node.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:35951482
      reference_title: 'Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies: from genetic heterogeneity to phenotypic continuum.'
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        characterized by early-onset, often severe epileptic seizures and EEG
        abnormalities
      explanation: >-
        Pairs the seizures and the EEG abnormality as joint characteristics of
        the DEE group, which is what this edge asserts.
  - target: Epileptic Encephalopathy Component
    description: >-
      Ongoing seizures and epileptiform activity themselves degrade cognitive
      and behavioural function.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:35951482
      reference_title: 'Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies: from genetic heterogeneity to phenotypic continuum.'
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        on a background of developmental impairment that tends to worsen as a
        consequence of epilepsy
      explanation: >-
        States that the epilepsy itself worsens developmental impairment, the
        defining claim of this causal edge.
- name: Impaired Synaptic Maturation and Neurodevelopment
  biological_scale: TISSUE
  description: >-
    Independent of seizure activity, the same channel or synaptic-gene
    defect disrupts activity-dependent synaptic pruning, circuit
    maturation, and neuronal migration/connectivity during critical
    developmental windows, producing a developmental encephalopathy
    component that is not fully reversible by seizure control alone.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39858526
    reference_title: 'Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy: Pathogenesis of Intellectual Disability Beyond Channelopathies.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      many other mechanisms have been identified: impaired neurogenesis,
      metabolic disorders, disruption of dendrite and axon growth, maintenance
      and synapse formation abnormalities -synaptopathies.
    explanation: >-
      Documents the non-channelopathy, neurodevelopmental mechanisms that
      constitute this seizure-independent arm of the DEE mechanism.
  downstream:
  - target: Developmental Encephalopathy Component
    description: >-
      Disrupted circuit maturation yields developmental delay and intellectual
      disability independently of seizure burden.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:39858526
      reference_title: 'Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy: Pathogenesis of Intellectual Disability Beyond Channelopathies.'
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        many other mechanisms have been identified: impaired neurogenesis,
        metabolic disorders, disruption of dendrite and axon growth, maintenance
        and synapse formation abnormalities -synaptopathies.
      explanation: >-
        Identifies the neurodevelopmental mechanisms that generate the
        developmental encephalopathy component.
- name: Epileptic Encephalopathy Component
  biological_scale: ORGANISM
  description: >-
    Frequent seizures and ongoing epileptiform discharges themselves
    contribute to cognitive slowing, developmental regression, and
    behavioral disturbance, over and above the effect of the underlying
    genetic lesion. This component can partially improve with effective
    seizure control.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:35951482
    reference_title: 'Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies: from genetic heterogeneity to phenotypic continuum.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      on a background of developmental impairment that tends to worsen as a
      consequence of epilepsy
    explanation: >-
      States the epileptic-encephalopathy component explicitly: the epilepsy
      itself worsens developmental impairment.
  - reference: PMID:28276062
    reference_title: 'ILAE classification of the epilepsies: Position paper of the ILAE Commission for Classification and Terminology.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      New terminology is introduced such as developmental and epileptic
      encephalopathy.
    explanation: >-
      The 2017 ILAE classification introduced the DEE term precisely to separate
      the epileptic from the developmental contribution to the encephalopathy.
  downstream:
  - target: Developmental Regression
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    description: >-
      What this component adds is deterioration: worsening of development on a
      background of established impairment, rather than the delay itself. That is
      why loss of previously acquired skills is routed from here rather than from
      the developmental component, which the entry treats as the source of the
      delay.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:35951482
      reference_title: 'Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies: from genetic heterogeneity to phenotypic continuum.'
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        on a background of developmental impairment that tends to worsen as a
        consequence of epilepsy
      explanation: >-
        States that the epilepsy itself worsens developmental impairment, which is
        the deterioration this edge asserts.
- name: Developmental Encephalopathy Component
  biological_scale: ORGANISM
  description: >-
    Developmental delay, intellectual disability, and often autistic
    features that arise directly from the genetic etiology's disruption of
    neurodevelopment, and that may be present even before seizure onset or
    persist despite adequate seizure control.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39858526
    reference_title: 'Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy: Pathogenesis of Intellectual Disability Beyond Channelopathies.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      What sets DEEs apart is their complex interplay of epilepsy and
      developmental delay, often driven by genetic factors. These two aspects
      influence one another but can develop independently, creating diagnostic
      and therapeutic challenges.
    explanation: >-
      Directly supports modeling the developmental component as a separate arm
      that can arise independently of the seizure burden - the conceptual basis
      for splitting these two nodes.
  downstream:
  - target: Developmental Delay
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    description: >-
      Delayed acquisition of milestones is the direct expression of this
      component, and in the DEE concept it may precede seizure onset.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:39858526
      reference_title: 'Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy: Pathogenesis of Intellectual Disability Beyond Channelopathies.'
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs) are a group of
        neuropediatric diseases associated with epileptic seizures, severe delay
        or regression of psychomotor development, and cognitive and behavioral
        deficits.
      explanation: >-
        Names severe delay of psychomotor development as a defining feature of the
        DEE group, alongside and separable from the seizures.
  - target: Intellectual Disability
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    description: >-
      The cognitive endpoint of the developmental arm. Its features may persist
      despite adequate seizure control, which is the clinical observation that
      makes this arm separable from the epileptic one.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:39858526
      reference_title: 'Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy: Pathogenesis of Intellectual Disability Beyond Channelopathies.'
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs) are a group of
        neuropediatric diseases associated with epileptic seizures, severe delay
        or regression of psychomotor development, and cognitive and behavioral
        deficits.
      explanation: >-
        Names cognitive deficits as a defining feature of the DEE group, alongside
        and separable from the seizures.
    - reference: PMID:39858526
      reference_title: 'Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy: Pathogenesis of Intellectual Disability Beyond Channelopathies.'
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: Intellectual disability is severe and complicates potential treatment.
      explanation: >-
        Characterises the severity of the intellectual disability this edge
        produces.
  - target: Autistic Behavior
    causal_link_type: UNKNOWN
    description: >-
      Autistic features are routed from the developmental rather than the
      epileptic arm because they are part of the cognitive and behavioural
      phenotype of the underlying genetic lesion. The sources cited here name
      autism spectrum disorder and behavioural deficits as features of the DEE
      group without attributing them to either arm, so the routing is this
      entry's model rather than a claim either source makes.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:39858526
      reference_title: 'Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy: Pathogenesis of Intellectual Disability Beyond Channelopathies.'
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs) are a group of
        neuropediatric diseases associated with epileptic seizures, severe delay
        or regression of psychomotor development, and cognitive and behavioral
        deficits.
      explanation: >-
        Names behavioural deficits as a feature of the DEE group. It does not
        separate the developmental from the epileptic contribution, hence INDIRECT.
    - reference: PMID:39237642
      reference_title: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        Patients have wide-ranging comorbidities including intellectual
        disability, psychiatric features, such as autism spectrum disorder and
        behavioural problems, movement and musculoskeletal disorders,
        gastrointestinal and sleep problems, together with  an increased
        mortality rate.
      explanation: >-
        Names autism spectrum disorder among the comorbidities of the DEE group.
        The review states co-occurrence and attributes no mechanism, hence INDIRECT.
  - target: Movement Disorder
    causal_link_type: UNKNOWN
    description: >-
      Movement disorders are routed from the developmental arm because most of
      the epilepsy-dyskinesia genes map to the same ion-channel and synaptic
      pathways as the upstream lesion nodes, rather than arising from the seizure
      burden. The cited review reports co-occurrence and gene-pathway membership;
      it does not test which arm produces the movement disorder, so this edge is
      an inference from the entry's two-component model.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:42068099
      reference_title: Movement Disorders in Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathies.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        Across DEE cohorts, movement disorders occurred in roughly one-quarter to
        over one-half of patients, were often hyperkinetic (notably dystonia and
        stereotypies), and frequently combined multiple phenomenologies.
      explanation: >-
        Quantifies movement disorders across DEE cohorts and gives their
        predominant hyperkinetic character. The review reports co-occurrence
        rather than a mechanism, hence INDIRECT.
    - reference: PMID:42068099
      reference_title: Movement Disorders in Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathies.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        Eight cohort studies and multiple tier 2-3 series and reviews yielded 245
        single-gene associations, most mapping to ion channel and synaptic
        signaling pathways.
      explanation: >-
        Places the epilepsy-dyskinesia gene set in the same ion-channel and
        synaptic classes as this entry's upstream lesion nodes, which is the basis
        for routing the movement disorder from the developmental arm.
- name: Genetic Lesion Beyond the Channelopathies
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  description: A large share of the genes in which pathogenic variants cause genetic DEE encode neither
    an ion channel nor a core synaptic protein, and the DEE literature explicitly separates these mechanisms
    from the channelopathies. The gene-defined subtypes wired at this node in this entry span Rac-GEF-dependent
    neuronal polarity (DOCK7), actin and protein-phosphatase-1 regulation in cortical migration (PHACTR1),
    receptor tyrosine kinase signalling (NTRK2), spliceosomal small nuclear RNA (RNU2-2), de-UFMylation
    (UFSP2), endoplasmic-reticulum stress signalling (RNF13), mitochondrial protein biosynthesis and
    mitochondrial trafficking (PARS2, TRAK1), purine metabolism and asparagine-linked glycosylation
    (ITPA, ALG13), endolysosomal acidification (ATP6V0A1), Na+/K+-ATPase pump function and neutral amino-acid
    transport (ATP1A2, SLC38A3), DNA repair (PNKP), and one gene in the 1q41-q42 microdeletion interval
    whose molecular function no reference cited here states (FBXO28). The DEE-series subtypes added
    under this parent extend that list with a Krebs cycle enzyme (MDH2), an endoplasmic-reticulum
    co-chaperone (CNPY3), a cut homeodomain transcription factor (CUX2), a cohesin subunit (SMC1A),
    a factor that targets arginine tRNAs for 3-methylcytosine modification (DALRD3), the v-ATPase A
    subunit (ATP6V1A), a nucleocytoplasmic shuttling RNA-binding protein (CELF2), a trans-Golgi network
    protein required for peptide hormone processing (HID1), a microtubule-associated serine-threonine
    kinase (MAST3), an inhibitory component of the mTOR pathway (DEPDC5), the anaphase-promoting complex
    subunit Cdh1 (FZR1), an ESCRT-II subunit (SNF8), the BRCA1-associated ATM activator (BRAT1), and the
    neuron-specific beta subunit of the AP-3 vesicle coat adaptor (AP3B2). AP3B2 is placed here rather
    than at the synaptic node because the AP-3 complex acts in organelle and vesicle biogenesis rather
    than at the synapse itself. Each functional assignment is
    taken from the publication cited on that subtype's own has_subtypes row. The node is kept separate
    from the ion-channel and synaptic lesion node because the two classes reach the shared excitation-inhibition
    and neurodevelopmental arms by different routes, not because the subtypes here are milder.

    supports: SUPPORT
