    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: 'many other mechanisms have been identified: impaired neurogenesis, metabolic disorders,
      disruption of dendrite and axon growth, maintenance and synapse formation abnormalities -synaptopathies.'
    explanation: Names the non-channelopathy mechanism classes that this node collects, in the review
      the entry already uses for the two-component DEE model.
  - reference: PMID:35951482
    reference_title: 'Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies: from genetic heterogeneity to
      phenotypic continuum.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Genetic DEEs have been associated with mutations in many genes involved in different
      functions including cell migration, proliferation, and organization, neuronal excitability,
      and synapse transmission and plasticity.
    explanation: Supports the breadth of gene functions represented at this node, including cell migration
      and organization.
  downstream:
  - target: Impaired Synaptic Maturation and Neurodevelopment
    description: A lesion in metabolic, transport, proteostasis, RNA-processing, cytoskeletal or genome-maintenance
      machinery disrupts circuit maturation directly, producing the developmental arm without requiring
      a primary change in channel conduction.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:39858526
      reference_title: 'Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy: Pathogenesis of Intellectual Disability
        Beyond Channelopathies.'
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: 'many other mechanisms have been identified: impaired neurogenesis, metabolic disorders,
        disruption of dendrite and axon growth, maintenance and synapse formation abnormalities -synaptopathies.'
      explanation: States that impaired neurogenesis, metabolic disorders and disrupted dendrite and
        axon growth are DEE mechanisms, which is the claim this edge makes.
  - target: Neuronal Excitation-Inhibition Imbalance
    description: The same non-channel lesions also reach excitation-inhibition balance, either by
      limiting the supply of neurotransmitter precursors and the ion gradients that neuronal firing
      depends on, or by altering neuronal excitability directly.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:35951482
      reference_title: 'Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies: from genetic heterogeneity to
        phenotypic continuum.'
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: Genetic DEEs have been associated with mutations in many genes involved in different
        functions including cell migration, proliferation, and organization, neuronal excitability,
        and synapse transmission and plasticity.
      explanation: Places neuronal excitability among the functions disrupted by the wider set of
        genetic DEE genes, supporting this edge from a non-channel lesion.

phenotypes:
- name: Developmental Delay
  category: Neurologic
  description: >-
    Developmental slowing or frank regression, which by definition of the DEE
    concept may precede, coincide with, or follow seizure onset.
  frequency: VERY_FREQUENT
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Global developmental delay
    term:
      id: HP:0001263
      label: Global developmental delay
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39237642
    reference_title: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      characterised by seizures and frequent epileptiform activity associated
      with developmental slowing or
    explanation: >-
      Developmental slowing or regression is a defining, near-universal feature
      of the DEE group.
- name: Intellectual Disability
  category: Neurologic
  frequency: VERY_FREQUENT
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Intellectual disability
    term:
      id: HP:0001249
      label: Intellectual disability
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39237642
    reference_title: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Patients have wide-ranging comorbidities including intellectual
      disability, psychiatric
    explanation: >-
      Intellectual disability is listed first among the wide-ranging
      comorbidities of the DEE group.
- name: Drug-Resistant Seizures
  category: Neurologic
  description: >-
    Multiple seizure types that are typically refractory to antiseizure
    medication, a defining feature of the DEE group.
  frequency: VERY_FREQUENT
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Seizure
    term:
      id: HP:0001250
      label: Seizure
    temporality: CHRONIC
    clinical_course: PROGRESSIVE
    onset:
      onset_category: INFANTILE
      notes: >-
        Onset is gene-dependent, spanning neonatal (KCNQ2, STXBP1, SCN2A/SCN8A
        gain-of-function) through early infantile (SCN1A, CDKL5) to later
        infancy and early childhood (PCDH19). Infantile onset is the modal
        category across the group.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40013914
    reference_title: Operational definition of developmental and epileptic encephalopathies to underpin the design of therapeutic trials.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs) are the most severe
      group of epilepsies, characterized by drug-resistant seizures and
      developmental slowing or regression.
    explanation: >-
      Drug resistance is part of the ILAE operational definition of the DEE
      group.
  sequelae:
  - target: Premature Mortality
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    description: >-
      Sudden unexpected death in epilepsy accounted for 19 of 42 deaths in a
      510-patient genetic DEE cohort, so ongoing seizures are a proximate route
      from this phenotype to premature death.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:36750385
      reference_title: Rates of Status Epilepticus and Sudden Unexplained Death in Epilepsy in People With Genetic Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathies.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: Cases of SUDEP accounted for 19/42 (48%) deaths.
      explanation: >-
        Quantifies the share of deaths attributable to sudden unexpected death in
        epilepsy, which is the seizure-mediated route this edge asserts.
- name: Status Epilepticus
  category: Neurologic
  description: >-
    Convulsive and nonconvulsive status epilepticus are frequent and
    life-threatening complications, affecting roughly half and one fifth of
    patients respectively across genetic DEE cohorts, with the highest burden in
    SCN1A-related disease.
  frequency: FREQUENT
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Status epilepticus
    term:
      id: HP:0002133
      label: Status epilepticus
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:36750385
    reference_title: Rates of Status Epilepticus and Sudden Unexplained Death in Epilepsy in People With Genetic Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The cohort comprised 510 individuals with a genetic DEE, in whom we
      observed CSE in 47% and NCSE in 19%.
    explanation: >-
      Quantifies convulsive and nonconvulsive status epilepticus in a large
      cohort restricted to genetic DEE, making it directly on-scope for this
      umbrella entry.
  - reference: PMID:36750385
    reference_title: Rates of Status Epilepticus and Sudden Unexplained Death in Epilepsy in People With Genetic Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The highest proportion of CSE occurred in
      patients with SCN1A-associated DEEs, including 181/203 (89%; 95% CI 84-93)
      patients with Dravet syndrome
    explanation: >-
      Documents the gene-dependent variation in status epilepticus risk, highest
      in SCN1A-related disease.
- name: Developmental Regression
  category: Neurologic
  description: >-
    Loss of previously acquired developmental skills, distinct from static
    delay. Regression is the more severe pole of the developmental
    encephalopathy component and is part of the operational definition of DEE.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Developmental regression
    term:
      id: HP:0002376
      label: Developmental regression
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40013914
    reference_title: Operational definition of developmental and epileptic encephalopathies to underpin the design of therapeutic trials.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      characterized by drug-resistant seizures and developmental slowing
      or regression
    explanation: >-
      Developmental regression is named in the ILAE operational definition of
      the DEE group.
  - reference: PMID:40831798
    reference_title: Progress of ketogenic diet in the treatment of developmental epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      It
      is characterized by early-onset, drug-resistant epilepsy, abnormal
      electroencephalogram (EEG) findings, and developmental delay or regression.
    explanation: >-

      of DEE.

genetic:
- name: Genetic Heterogeneity Across Ion Channel and Synaptic Genes
  notes: >-
    Pathogenic variants causing genetic DEE have been reported in more than nine
    hundred genes; the most frequent recurring categories are voltage-gated ion
    channel genes (SCN1A, SCN2A, SCN8A, KCNQ2, KCNA2, KCNT1), presynaptic
    vesicle-cycle genes (STXBP1, DNM1, SNAP25), and postsynaptic
    neurotransmitter-receptor genes (GRIN1, GRIN2A, GRIN2B), with most cases
    arising from de novo dominant variants. Individual gene-defined forms are
    curated as separate dismech entries.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39237642
    reference_title: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      genetic cause is found in >50% of patients using next generation
      sequencing technologies.
    explanation: >-
      Establishes that a genetic etiology is identified in the majority of DEE
      patients, justifying the genetic DEE umbrella as the dominant subgroup.

  gene_term:

    case_fraction_percent: 5.6
    cohort_size: 1568
    notes: Second most frequently reported gene in the Italian national survey.

    - reference: PMID:39613335

      snippet: >-

        followed by KCNQ2 (5.6%) and SCN2A (5%).
      explanation: >-
        Quantifies the KCNQ2 share of molecularly diagnosed genetic DEE cases.
  evidence:

    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      KCNQ2, CDKL5, SCN1A, and STXBP1 were the most frequently identified genes.
    explanation: >-
      Identifies KCNQ2 among the most frequently identified causal genes in a
      clinical DEE exome cohort.

  notes: >-

  gene_term:

    loss-of-function variants give a later-onset, autism-predominant phenotype.

    term:
      id: hgnc:800
      label: ATP1A2
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE98
  notes: One of the two Na+/K+-ATPase alpha-subunit isoforms implicated in this spectrum. Heterozygous
    variants that severely impair pump activity cause a profound epileptic encephalopathy with polymicrogyria
    or progressive brain atrophy, distinct from the familial hemiplegic migraine and alternating hemiplegia
    phenotypes curated in other dismech entries.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33880529
    reference_title: ATP1A2- and ATP1A3-associated early profound epileptic encephalopathy and polymicrogyria.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: We tested 14 mutations in transfected COS-1 cells and demonstrated impaired NKA-pump
      activity, consistent with severe loss of function.
    explanation: Establishes loss of Na+/K+-ATPase pump function as the molecular consequence.
- name: FBXO28
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: FBXO28
    term:
      id: hgnc:29046
      label: FBXO28
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE100
  notes: HGNC names this gene F-box protein 28. It is one of the two genes in the 1q41-q42 microdeletion
    interval already implicated in monogenic disease, and heterozygous variants cause DEE with profound
    intellectual disability and hyperkinetic movement disorders.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33280099
    reference_title: FBXO28 causes developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with profound intellectual
      disability.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We describe nine new patients with FBXO28 pathogenic variants (four missense, including
      one recurrent, three nonsense, and one frameshift) and analyze all 10 known cases to delineate
      the phenotypic spectrum. All patients had epilepsy and 9 of 10 had DEE, including infantile
      spasms (3) and a progressive myoclonic epilepsy (1).
    explanation: Establishes FBXO28 as a monogenic cause of DEE.
- name: SLC38A3
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: SLC38A3
    term:
      id: hgnc:18044
      label: SLC38A3
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE102
  notes: SNAT3, a sodium-coupled neutral amino acid transporter. Biallelic variants perturb glutamine
    homeostasis; glutamine is the precursor of both GABA and glutamate, which is how this transport
    lesion reaches excitation-inhibition balance.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34605855
    reference_title: Biallelic variants in SLC38A3 encoding a glutamine transporter cause epileptic
      encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Our data support the contention that SLC38A3 is a novel disease gene for developmental
      and epileptic encephalopathy and illuminate the likely pathophysiology of the disease as perturbations
      in glutamine homeostasis.
    explanation: Establishes SLC38A3 as a DEE gene acting through glutamine homeostasis.
- name: ATP6V0A1
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: ATP6V0A1
    term:
      id: hgnc:865
      label: ATP6V0A1
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE104
  notes: Subunit a1 of the V0 domain of the vacuolar H+-ATPase, the brain-enriched isoform. De novo
    missense variants cause severe DEE, while biallelic variants give progressive myoclonus epilepsy
    with ataxia; the recurrent R740Q change impairs endolysosomal acidification.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34909687
    reference_title: Variants in ATP6V0A1 cause progressive myoclonus epilepsy and developmental and
      epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Five affected subjects with biallelic variants in this gene presented with a phenotype
      of early-onset progressive myoclonus epilepsy with ataxia, while 12 individuals carried de novo
      missense variants and showed severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
    explanation: Establishes ATP6V0A1 as causal for DEE and records the genotype-phenotype split.
- name: UFSP2
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: UFSP2
    term:
      id: hgnc:25640
      label: UFSP2
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE106
  notes: UFM1-specific peptidase 2, a de-UFMylating enzyme. Homozygosity for the N-terminal-domain
    p.V115E variant causes a severe neurodevelopmental disability with epilepsy, distinct from the
    autosomal dominant skeletal dysplasias caused by catalytic-domain variants.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33473208
    reference_title: A pathogenic UFSP2 variant in an autosomal recessive form of pediatric neurodevelopmental
      anomalies and epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Different UFSP2 variants cause markedly different diseases, with homozygosity for V115E
      causing a severe syndrome of neurodevelopmental disability and epilepsy.
    explanation: Establishes the recessive UFSP2 neurodevelopmental phenotype as a distinct disease
      from the dominant skeletal one.
- name: CACNA2D1
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: CACNA2D1
    term:
      id: hgnc:1399
      label: CACNA2D1
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE110
  notes: α2δ-1 auxiliary subunit of CaV1 and CaV2 voltage-gated calcium channels. Biallelic loss-of-function
    variants severely impair its function as a calcium channel subunit and cause early-onset DEE.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:35293990
    reference_title: Biallelic CACNA2D1 loss-of-function variants cause early-onset developmental
      epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Thus, biallelic loss-of-function variants in CACNA2D1 underlie the severe neurodevelopmental
      disorder in these two patients.
    explanation: Establishes biallelic CACNA2D1 loss of function as causal, placing the lesion in
      the calcium-channel arm.
- name: SV2A
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: SV2A
    term:
      id: hgnc:20566
      label: SV2A
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE113
  notes: Synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A and the binding site of levetiracetam. A single homozygous
    R383Q missense variant in one consanguineous family is the whole reported basis of this subtype;
    levetiracetam was ineffective in the proband.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:26002053
    reference_title: Homozygous Mutation in Synaptic Vesicle Glycoprotein 2A Gene Results in Intractable
      Epilepsy, Involuntary Movements, Microcephaly, and Developmental and Growth Retardation.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Levetiracetam, which binds to SV2A, was not effective as an antiepileptic medication.
    explanation: Records that the drug whose target this gene encodes did not control the proband's
      seizures.
- name: RNU2-2
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: RNU2-2
    term:
      id: hgnc:10152
      label: RNU2-2P
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE119
  notes: U2-2 small nuclear RNA of the major spliceosome. HGNC renamed this locus from RNU2-2P to
    RNU2-2 on 2024-11-15 (live HGNC REST lookup for HGNC:10152 returns symbol RNU2-2 with RNU2-2P
    as a previous symbol); the OBO HGNC build this repository validates against still carries RNU2-2P,
    so term.label is the build's label while preferred_term is the current approved symbol. Recurrent
    de novo variants at nucleotide positions 4 and 35 cause DEE119; no missplicing was detected in
    patient blood.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40210679
    reference_title: Mutations in the small nuclear RNA gene RNU2-2 cause a severe neurodevelopmental
      disorder with prominent epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Here, we report that recurrent germline mutations in RNU2-2 (previously known as pseudogene
      RNU2-2P), a 191-bp gene that encodes the U2-2 snRNA, are responsible for a related disorder.
    explanation: Establishes the gene, its former pseudogene designation, and its causal role.
- name: BAIAP2
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: BAIAP2
    term:
      id: hgnc:947
      label: BAIAP2
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE120
  notes: Brain-specific angiogenesis inhibitor 1-associated protein 2, acting in dendritic spine morphogenesis
    and excitatory synapse formation. De novo missense variants clustered in the multiple phosphorylation
    site region act by gain of function, increasing excitatory synaptogenesis and neuronal excitability.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:41133935
    reference_title: De novo missense variants in BAIAP2 are associated with developmental and epileptic
      encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Using whole exome/genome sequencing, we identified de novo missense variants in BAIAP2
      in six patients with DEEs.
    explanation: Establishes BAIAP2 as a causal DEE gene.
- name: LGI1
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: LGI1
    term:
      id: hgnc:6572
      label: LGI1
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE121
  notes: Leucine-rich glioma-inactivated protein 1, a secreted ligand for ADAM22 and ADAM23. Biallelic
    variants that reduce secretion and ADAM22 binding cause DEE121; monoallelic variants cause autosomal
    dominant epilepsy with auditory features, curated in the Autosomal_Dominant_Epilepsy_with_Auditory_Features
    entry.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40455867
    reference_title: Biallelic LGI1 and ADAM23 variants cause hippocampal epileptic encephalopathy
      via the LGI1-ADAM22/23 pathway.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: LGI1 is a secreted neuronal protein, functions as a ligand for ADAM22/23, and regulates
      excitatory synaptic transmission and neuronal excitability in the brain.
    explanation: States the synaptic mechanism through which the LGI1 lesion reaches neuronal excitability.
- name: PNKP
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: PNKP
    term:
      id: hgnc:9154
      label: PNKP
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: MCSZ
  notes: Polynucleotide kinase 3'-phosphatase. Biallelic variants cause MCSZ; a splicing allele is
    associated with a milder course. The allelic PNKP peripheral-nerve phenotype is curated in Charcot-Marie-Tooth_Disease_Type_2B2.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:20118933
    reference_title: Mutations in PNKP cause microcephaly, seizures and defects in DNA repair.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: we mapped the disease locus to chromosome 19q13.33 and identified multiple mutations
      in PNKP (polynucleotide kinase 3'-phosphatase) that result in severe neurological disease; in
      contrast, a splicing mutation is associated with more moderate symptoms.
    explanation: Establishes PNKP as the causal gene and records the allele-dependent severity.

- name: SCN3A
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: SCN3A
    term:
      id: hgnc:10590
      label: SCN3A
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE62
  notes: HGNC names this gene sodium voltage-gated channel alpha subunit 3. The cited report identifies
    Nav1.3 as highly expressed in brain and previously unlinked to early infantile epileptic encephalopathy;
    de novo missense variants produce gain of channel function.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29466837
    reference_title: Mutations in SCN3A cause early infantile epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Here, we describe a cohort of 4 patients with epileptic encephalopathy and heterozygous de
      novo missense variants in SCN3A (p.Ile875Thr in 2 cases, p.Pro1333Leu, and p.Val1769Ala).
    explanation: Establishes SCN3A as causal for DEE62.
- name: KCNC2
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: KCNC2
    term:
      id: hgnc:6234
      label: KCNC2
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE103
  notes: HGNC names this gene potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily C member 2. The cited report describes
    Kv3.2 as a Shaw-related voltage-gated potassium channel subunit important for sustained high-frequency
    firing; the DEE pole of the KCNC2 spectrum is associated with gain of function.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:35314505
    reference_title: Spectrum of Phenotypic, Genetic, and Functional Characteristics in Patients With
      Epilepsy With KCNC2 Pathogenic Variants.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We identified novel KCNC2 variants in 18 patients with various forms of epilepsy, including
      genetic generalized epilepsy (GGE), developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) including early-onset
      absence epilepsy, focal epilepsy, and myoclonic-atonic epilepsy.
    explanation: Establishes KCNC2 as causal across a spectrum whose severe pole is DEE103.
- name: KCNH5
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: KCNH5
    term:
      id: hgnc:6254
      label: KCNH5
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE112
  notes: HGNC names this gene potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily H member 5. The cited report describes
    KCNH5 as encoding the voltage-gated potassium channel EAG2/Kv10.2; the DEE phenotype is associated
    with specific recurrent variants rather than with the gene as a whole.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:36307226
    reference_title: Neurodevelopmental and Epilepsy Phenotypes in Individuals With Missense Variants
      in the Voltage-Sensing and Pore Domains of KCNH5.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We report a cohort of 17 patients, including 9 with a recurrent de novo missense variant
      p.Arg327His, 4 with a recurrent missense variant p.Arg333His, and 4 additional novel missense variants.
    explanation: Establishes the KCNH5 variant series behind DEE112.
- name: KCNT2
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: KCNT2
    term:
      id: hgnc:18866
      label: KCNT2
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE57
  notes: HGNC names this gene potassium sodium-activated channel subfamily T member 2. The paralogue of
    KCNT1. De novo variants act by gain of function and were quinidine-responsive in vitro and in one
    treated patient.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29740868
    reference_title: De novo gain-of-function variants in KCNT2 as a novel cause of developmental and
      epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We report on 2 females with de novo variants in KCNT2 with West syndrome followed by Lennox-Gastaut
      syndrome or with DEE with migrating focal seizures.
    explanation: Establishes KCNT2 as causal for DEE57.
- name: TMEM63B
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: TMEM63B
    term:
      id: hgnc:17735
      label: TMEM63B
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE118
  notes: HGNC names this gene transmembrane protein 63B. The cited report describes TMEM63B as a highly
    conserved stretch-activated ion channel; the mutated channels carry an inward leak cation current
    under isotonic conditions.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:37421948
    reference_title: Stretch-activated ion channel TMEM63B associates with developmental and epileptic
      encephalopathies and progressive neurodegeneration.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Here, we describe 17 unrelated individuals with severe early-onset developmental and epileptic
      encephalopathy (DEE), intellectual disability, and severe motor and cortical visual impairment associated
      with progressive neurodegenerative brain changes carrying ten distinct heterozygous variants of
      TMEM63B, encoding for a highly conserved stretch-activated ion channel.
    explanation: Establishes TMEM63B as causal for this DEE and names the channel class.
- name: GABRB2
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: GABRB2
    term:
      id: hgnc:4082
      label: GABRB2
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE92
  notes: HGNC names this gene gamma-aminobutyric acid type A receptor subunit beta2. One of eight genes
    given a causal link to DEE by the cited whole-genome study of unexplained DEE trios. That study characterises
    no GABRB2-specific phenotype.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29100083
    reference_title: High Rate of Recurrent De Novo Mutations in Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: 'By combining these strategies, we were able to provide a causal link between DEE and the
      following genes: NTRK2, GABRB2, CLTC, DHDDS, NUS1, RAB11A, GABBR2, and SNAP25.'
    explanation: Establishes GABRB2 as causal for DEE.
- name: GABRA2
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: GABRA2
    term:
      id: hgnc:4076
      label: GABRA2
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE78
  notes: HGNC names this gene gamma-aminobutyric acid type A receptor subunit alpha2. The cited report
    describes GABA-A receptors as ligand-gated anion channels regulating neuronal inhibition; the p.Thr292Lys
    variant reduced channel expression and left the channel tonically open in the absence of GABA.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29961870
    reference_title: De novo variants in GABRA2 and GABRA5 alter receptor function and contribute to early-onset
      epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Targeted resequencing of 279 additional epilepsy patients identified 19 rare variants from
      nine GABAA receptor genes, including a novel de novo missense variant in GABRA2 (c.875C > A, p.T292K)
      and a recurrent missense variant in GABRB3 (c.902C > T, p.P301L).
    explanation: Establishes the de novo GABRA2 variant causal for DEE78.
- name: GABRA5
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: GABRA5
    term:
      id: hgnc:4079
      label: GABRA5
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE79
  notes: HGNC names this gene gamma-aminobutyric acid type A receptor subunit alpha5. The p.Val294Leu
    variant raises GABA sensitivity tenfold but reduces the maximal GABA-evoked current through increased
    desensitisation, so the net effect is loss of sustained inhibition.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29961870
    reference_title: De novo variants in GABRA2 and GABRA5 alter receptor function and contribute to early-onset
      epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Using whole-genome sequencing, we identified a novel de novo missense variant in GABRA5 (c.880G
      > C, p.V294L) in a patient with severe early-onset epilepsy and developmental delay.
    explanation: Establishes the de novo GABRA5 variant causal for DEE79.
- name: GABBR2
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: GABBR2
    term:
      id: hgnc:4507
      label: GABBR2
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE59
  notes: HGNC names this gene gamma-aminobutyric acid type B receptor subunit 2. The metabotropic GABA-B
    receptor subunit, so a lesion of GABAergic inhibition rather than of a voltage-gated channel. First
    seen in two DEE trios as suggestive evidence; the causal link came from a later whole-genome study.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29100083
    reference_title: High Rate of Recurrent De Novo Mutations in Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: 'By combining these strategies, we were able to provide a causal link between DEE and the
      following genes: NTRK2, GABRB2, CLTC, DHDDS, NUS1, RAB11A, GABBR2, and SNAP25.'
    explanation: Establishes GABBR2 as causal for DEE.
- name: SLC32A1
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: SLC32A1
    term:
      id: hgnc:11018
      label: SLC32A1
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE114
  notes: HGNC names this gene solute carrier family 32 member 1. The cited report names SLC32A1 as the
    gene encoding the vesicular GABA transporter. Inherited missense variants cause genetic epilepsy with
    febrile seizures plus; de novo missense variants cause this DEE.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:36073542
    reference_title: De Novo Missense Variants in SLC32A1 Cause a Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy
      Due to Impaired GABAergic Neurotransmission.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Using exome sequencing, we identified four individuals with a developmental and epileptic
      encephalopathy and de novo missense variants in SLC32A1.
    explanation: Establishes de novo SLC32A1 variants as causal for DEE114.
- name: NSF
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: NSF
    term:
      id: hgnc:8016
      label: NSF
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE96
  notes: HGNC names this gene N-ethylmaleimide sensitive factor, vesicle fusing ATPase. The cited report
    describes NSF as critical for intracellular vesicle transport underlying neurotransmitter release,
    and reads the de novo variants as dominant negative on the strength of a Drosophila eye assay.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:31675180
    reference_title: De novo NSF mutations cause early infantile epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Herein, we, for the first time, document human monogenic disease phenotype of de novo pathogenic
      variants in NSF, that is, epileptic encephalopathy of early infantile onset.
    explanation: Establishes NSF as causal for DEE96.
- name: NAPB
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: NAPB
    term:
      id: hgnc:15751
      label: NAPB
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE107
  notes: HGNC names this gene NSF attachment protein beta. The beta attachment protein of NSF. The cited
    report places it in SNARE complex dissociation and recycling during synaptic vesicle docking, so NAPB
    and NSF are lesions at successive steps of one machinery.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:26235277
    reference_title: NAPB - a novel SNARE-associated protein for early-onset epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Variant prioritization identified a homozygous nonsense variant in the N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive
      factor attachment protein, beta (NAPB) gene resulting in a premature stop codon and 46% loss of
      the protein.
    explanation: Establishes the homozygous NAPB lesion causal for DEE107.
- name: SYNJ1
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: SYNJ1
    term:
      id: hgnc:11503
      label: SYNJ1
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE53
  notes: HGNC names this gene synaptojanin 1. A polyphosphoinositide phosphatase with two phosphatase
    domains acting in synaptic vesicle dynamics. Variants abolishing only Sac1 activity cause early-onset
    parkinsonism; a critical reduction of the dual activity causes this DEE.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:27435091
    reference_title: Loss of SYNJ1 dual phosphatase activity leads to early onset refractory seizures
      and progressive neurological decline.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We performed whole exome or genome sequencing in three independent sib pairs with early onset
      refractory seizures and progressive neurological decline, and identified novel segregating recessive
      SYNJ1 defects.
    explanation: Establishes recessive SYNJ1 defects as causal for DEE53.
- name: MDH2
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: MDH2
    term:
      id: hgnc:6971
      label: MDH2
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE51
  notes: HGNC names this gene malate dehydrogenase 2. Mitochondrial malate dehydrogenase, which converts
    malate to oxaloacetate in the Krebs cycle. Patient fibroblasts lost MDH2 protein with enzymatic activity
    close to null and accumulated malate and fumarate.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:27989324
    reference_title: Mutations in MDH2, Encoding a Krebs Cycle Enzyme, Cause Early-Onset Severe Encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We report bi-allelic pathogenic mutations in MDH2 in three unrelated subjects presenting
      with early-onset generalized hypotonia, psychomotor delay, refractory epilepsy, and elevated lactate
      in the blood and cerebrospinal fluid.
    explanation: Establishes biallelic MDH2 variants as causal for DEE51.
- name: CNPY3
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: CNPY3
    term:
      id: hgnc:11968
      label: CNPY3
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE60
  notes: HGNC names this gene canopy FGF signaling regulator 3. An endoplasmic reticulum co-chaperone
    that regulates the subcellular distribution and responses of multiple Toll-like receptors. Protein
    was severely reduced in lymphoblastoid cells from two affected siblings.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29394991
    reference_title: Biallelic Variants in CNPY3, Encoding an Endoplasmic Reticulum Chaperone, Cause Early-Onset
      Epileptic Encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We have now identified biallelic CNPY3 variants in three individuals with WS; these include
      compound-heterozygous missense and frameshift variants in a family with two affected siblings (individuals
      1 and 2) and a homozygous splicing variant in a consanguineous family (individual 3).
    explanation: Establishes biallelic CNPY3 variants as causal for DEE60.
- name: CUX2
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: CUX2
    term:
      id: hgnc:19347
      label: CUX2
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE67
  notes: HGNC names this gene cut like homeobox 2. A cut homeodomain transcription factor with a role
    in dendrite branching, spine development and synapse formation in layer II to III cortical neurons.
    The recurrent p.Glu590Lys variant lies in the CUT domain and is predicted to interfere with DNA binding.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29630738
    reference_title: The epilepsy phenotypic spectrum associated with a recurrent CUX2 variant.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We identify a recurrent de novo CUX2 p.Glu590Lys as a novel genetic cause for developmental
      and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE).
    explanation: Establishes the recurrent CUX2 variant as causal for DEE67.
- name: SMC1A
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: SMC1A
    term:
      id: hgnc:11111
      label: SMC1A
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE85
  notes: HGNC names this gene structural maintenance of chromosomes 1A. A core structural subunit of the
    cohesin complex, so this is a cohesinopathy. Missense and small in-frame changes cause about 5 per
    cent of Cornelia de Lange syndrome, curated separately; protein-truncating changes cause this X-linked
    epilepsy phenotype.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:28166369
    reference_title: 'Heterozygous truncation mutations of the SMC1A gene cause a severe early onset epilepsy
      with cluster seizures in females: Detailed phenotyping of 10 new cases.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Ten cases with heterozygous de novo mutations in the SMC1A gene are presented. All 10 mutations
      identified are predicted to result in premature truncation of the SMC1A protein.
    explanation: Establishes truncating SMC1A variants as causal for DEE85.
- name: DALRD3
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: DALRD3
    term:
      id: hgnc:25536
      label: DALRD3
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE86
  notes: HGNC names this gene DALR anticodon binding domain containing 3. Forms a complex with the METTL2
    methyltransferase that selects particular arginine tRNA isoacceptors for 3-methylcytosine modification
    of the anticodon loop.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:32427860
    reference_title: DALRD3 encodes a protein mutated in epileptic encephalopathy that targets arginine
      tRNAs for 3-methylcytosine modification.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Notably, we identify a homozygous nonsense mutation in the DALRD3 gene that impairs m3C formation
      in human patients exhibiting developmental delay and early-onset epileptic encephalopathy.
    explanation: Establishes the homozygous DALRD3 lesion as causal for DEE86 and names the tRNA-modification
      defect.
- name: ATP6V1A
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: ATP6V1A
    term:
      id: hgnc:851
      label: ATP6V1A
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE93
  notes: HGNC names this gene ATPase H+ transporting V1 subunit A. The A subunit of the vacuolar proton
    ATPase, which sets organellar pH and has additional roles at the neuronal synapse. Severity in the
    founding four patients tracked the individual variant.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29668857
    reference_title: De novo mutations of the ATP6V1A gene cause developmental encephalopathy with epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Through whole exome sequencing, we identified de novo heterozygous mutations (p.Pro27Arg,
      p.Asp100Tyr, p.Asp349Asn, p.Asp371Gly) in ATP6V1A, encoding the A subunit of v-ATPase, in four patients
      with developmental encephalopathy with epilepsy.
    explanation: Establishes de novo ATP6V1A variants as causal for DEE93.
- name: CELF2
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: CELF2
    term:
      id: hgnc:2550
      label: CELF2
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE97
  notes: HGNC names this gene CUGBP Elav-like family member 2. A nucleocytoplasmic shuttling RNA-binding
    protein with roles in RNA processing and in development of the central nervous system and heart. The
    pathogenic variants cluster at the C-terminal nuclear localisation signal and mislocalise the protein
    out of the nucleus.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33131106
    reference_title: De novo variants in CELF2 that disrupt the nuclear localization signal cause developmental
      and epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: 'We report heterozygous CELF2 (NM_006561.3) variants in five unrelated individuals: Individuals
      1-4 exhibited developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) and Individual 5 had intellectual
      disability and autistic features.'
    explanation: Establishes heterozygous CELF2 variants as causal for DEE97.
- name: HID1
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: HID1
    term:
      id: hgnc:15736
      label: HID1
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE105
  notes: HGNC names this gene HID1 domain containing. Acts in the trans-Golgi network where peptide hormone
    precursors are processed, which is why the biallelic lesion pairs an epileptic encephalopathy with
    central pituitary insufficiency.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33999436
    reference_title: Mutations in HID1 Cause Syndromic Infantile Encephalopathy and Hypopituitarism.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Bi-allelic variants in the gene HID1 domain-containing protein 1 (HID1) were identified in
      all patients.
    explanation: Establishes biallelic HID1 variants as causal for DEE105.
- name: MAST3
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: MAST3
    term:
      id: hgnc:19036
      label: MAST3
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE108
  notes: HGNC names this gene microtubule associated serine/threonine kinase 3. One of the microtubule-associated
    serine-threonine kinases, expressed in excitatory cortical neurons late in prenatal development and
    postnatally. Transfected cells showed increased phosphorylation of the MAST3 target ARPP-16, read
    as gain of function.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34185323
    reference_title: Pathogenic MAST3 Variants in the STK Domain Are Associated with Epilepsy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We identify de novo missense variants in the STK domain in 11 individuals, including 2 recurrent
      variants p.G510S (n = 5) and p.G515S (n = 3).
    explanation: Establishes de novo MAST3 kinase-domain variants as causal for DEE108.
- name: DEPDC5
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: DEPDC5
    term:
      id: hgnc:18423
      label: DEPDC5
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE111
  notes: HGNC names this gene DEP domain containing 5, GATOR1 subcomplex subunit. An inhibitory component
    of the mTOR pathway. The common germline lesion is a single inactivating heterozygous variant, curated
    as the separate DEPDC5-Related_Epilepsy entry; the biallelic germline lesion curated here gives bilateral
    polymicrogyria with macrocephaly instead of a focal lesion.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:36067010
    reference_title: Germline homozygous missense DEPDC5 variants cause severe refractory early-onset
      epilepsy, macrocephaly and bilateral polymicrogyria.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We describe a novel phenotype caused by germline biallelic missense variants in DEPDC5.
    explanation: Establishes germline biallelic DEPDC5 variants as causal for DEE111 and separates them
      from the heterozygous focal-epilepsy phenotype.
- name: FZR1
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: FZR1
    term:
      id: hgnc:24824
      label: FZR1
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE109
  notes: HGNC names this gene fizzy and cell division cycle 20 related 1. Encodes Cdh1, a substrate-recognition
    subunit of the anaphase-promoting complex, with roles in the cell cycle and in post-mitotic neurons.
    Drosophila assays supported the patient variants being loss of function.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34788397
    reference_title: De novo FZR1 loss-of-function variants cause developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: In this study, evaluation of 250 unrelated patients with developmental and epileptic encephalopathies
      and a connection on GeneMatcher led to the identification of three de novo missense variants in
      FZR1.
    explanation: Establishes de novo FZR1 variants as causal for DEE109.
- name: SNF8
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: SNF8
    term:
      id: hgnc:17028
      label: SNF8
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE115
  notes: HGNC names this gene SNF8 subunit of ESCRT-II. A subunit of ESCRT-II, one of the three endosomal
    sorting complexes required for membrane remodelling and autophagy. The milder pole of the SNF8 spectrum
    is curated as SNF8-Related_Neurodevelopmental_Disorder.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:38423010
    reference_title: Bi-allelic variants in SNF8 cause a disease spectrum ranging from severe developmental
      and epileptic encephalopathy to syndromic optic atrophy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: 'We report nine individuals from six families presenting with a spectrum of neurodevelopmental/neurodegenerative
      features caused by bi-allelic variants in SNF8 (GenBank: NM_007241.4), encoding the ESCRT-II subunit
      SNF8.'
    explanation: Establishes biallelic SNF8 variants as causal across the spectrum whose severe pole is
      DEE115.
- name: BRAT1
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: BRAT1
    term:
      id: hgnc:21701
      label: BRAT1
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: RMFSL
  notes: 'HGNC names this gene BRCA1 associated ATM activator 1. Biallelic variants give two distinct
    phenotypes, and the genotype largely predicts which: nonsense, frameshift or in-frame indel genotypes
    give the lethal rigidity and multifocal-seizure phenotype, while genotypes including a missense variant
    usually give the non-lethal cerebellar-atrophy phenotype.'
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:37344571
    reference_title: 'BRAT1-related disorders: phenotypic spectrum and phenotype-genotype correlations
      from 97 patients.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Genotype-phenotype correlations in our cohort revealed that biallelic nonsense, frameshift
      or inframe deletion/insertion variants result in the severe BRAT1-related RMFSL phenotype (46/46;
      100%). In contrast, genotypes with at least one missense were more likely associated with NEDCAS
      (28/34; 82%).
    explanation: Establishes the BRAT1 genotype-phenotype split that assigns this gene to the lethal phenotype
      curated here.
- name: AP3B2
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: AP3B2
    term:
      id: hgnc:567
      label: AP3B2
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  subtype: DEE48
  notes: HGNC names this gene adaptor related protein complex 3 subunit beta 2. The neuron-specific beta
    subunit of the AP-3 vesicle coat adaptor complex. The ubiquitous isoform AP3B1 causes Hermansky-Pudlak
    syndrome type 2 instead, which is why the AP3B2 phenotype is purely neurological.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:27889060
    reference_title: Autosomal-Recessive Mutations in AP3B2, Adaptor-Related Protein Complex 3 Beta 2
      Subunit, Cause an Early-Onset Epileptic Encephalopathy with Optic Atrophy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: AP3B2 encodes the neuron-specific subunit of the AP-3 complex.
    explanation: Names the gene product whose loss produces DEE48, and the neuronal restriction that confines
      the phenotype to the nervous system.
treatments:
- name: Anti-Seizure Medication
  description: >-
    Broad-spectrum and gene-informed anti-seizure medication selection,
    guided where possible by the specific ion-channel gain- versus
    loss-of-function mechanism (e.g. sodium-channel blockers are often
    beneficial in SCN2A/SCN8A gain-of-function DEE but can worsen seizures
    in SCN1A-related Dravet syndrome loss-of-function disease).
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pharmacotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15986
      label: Pharmacotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: anticonvulsant agent
      term:
        id: NCIT:C264
        label: Anticonvulsant Agent
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Hypersynchronous Network Activity and Seizures
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
    description: >-
      Antiseizure medication suppresses the seizure-generating network activity.
      Which agent helps versus harms is determined by the upstream channel
      lesion: sodium-channel blockers benefit SCN2A/SCN8A gain-of-function
      disease but worsen SCN1A loss-of-function Dravet syndrome.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:39237642
      reference_title: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        Understanding the functional consequences of the SCN1A pathogenic
        variant informs management, as some sodium channel blocker (SCB)
        antiseizure medications (ASMs) may exacerbate seizures in Dravet
        syndrome, whereas patients with the non-Dravet, EIDEE phenotype due to
        GOF variants may respond to SCB, such as carbamazepine and phenytoin
      explanation: >-
        Directly supports the gain- versus loss-of-function prescribing logic
        stated in this mechanism description: sodium-channel blockers exacerbate
        seizures in SCN1A loss-of-function Dravet syndrome but benefit
        gain-of-function disease. This is the entry's most clinically
        consequential claim and is now cited rather than resting on notes.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39237642
    reference_title: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Holistic management, which
      encompasses antiseizure therapies and care for multimorbidities, is
      determined both by epilepsy syndrome and aetiology.
    explanation: >-
      Supports antiseizure therapy as the pharmacological cornerstone, with
      choice determined by syndrome and aetiology.
- name: Ketogenic Diet
  description: >-
    Dietary therapy used as an adjunct or alternative treatment for
    drug-resistant seizures in genetic DEE, with demonstrated efficacy across
    several DEE subtypes and occasional reduction of pharmacological need.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: dietary intervention
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15447
      label: Dietary Intervention
  therapeutic_modality: BEHAVIORAL
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Hypersynchronous Network Activity and Seizures
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
    description: >-
      Ketogenic dietary therapy suppresses the seizure-generating network
      activity rather than correcting the upstream genetic lesion.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:40831798
      reference_title: Progress of ketogenic diet in the treatment of developmental epileptic encephalopathy.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        The ketogenic diet
        (KD) is a well-established non-pharmacological treatment for refractory
        epilepsy and has demonstrated therapeutic efficacy in several DEE
        subtypes.
      explanation: >-
        Supports the seizure-directed effect of dietary therapy across DEE
        subtypes.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40831798
    reference_title: Progress of ketogenic diet in the treatment of developmental epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The ketogenic diet
      (KD) is a well-established non-pharmacological treatment for refractory
      epilepsy and has demonstrated therapeutic efficacy in several DEE
      subtypes.
    explanation: >-
      DEE-specific review establishing ketogenic diet efficacy across DEE
      subtypes.
  - reference: PMID:40831798
    reference_title: Progress of ketogenic diet in the treatment of developmental epileptic encephalopathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      In certain
      cases, it may reduce or even eliminate the need for pharmacological
      interventions.
    explanation: >-
      Documents that dietary therapy can reduce antiseizure medication burden in
      some patients.
- name: Cannabidiol
  description: >-
    Randomised placebo-controlled trials demonstrated efficacy in Dravet
    syndrome, Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, and tuberous sclerosis complex, with
    median target-seizure reductions of 38.9%, 41.9%, and 48.6% respectively.
    One of the few DEE therapies supported by RCT-level evidence.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pharmacotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15986
      label: Pharmacotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: cannabidiol
      term:
        id: CHEBI:69478
        label: cannabidiol
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Hypersynchronous Network Activity and Seizures
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
    description: >-
      Symptomatic suppression of seizure generation; does not address the
      developmental arm of the mechanism.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:39237642
      reference_title: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        Randomised placebo-controlled trials (RCTs) of cannabidiol demonstrated
        efficacy
        in Dravet syndrome , LGS and TSC, with significant median percent
        reduction s in target seizures
      explanation: >-
        RCT evidence that the effect is on target seizures, i.e. the seizure
        node of the pathograph.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39237642
    reference_title: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Randomised placebo-controlled trials (RCTs) of cannabidiol demonstrated
      efficacy
      in Dravet syndrome , LGS and TSC, with significant median percent
      reduction s in target seizures
    explanation: >-
      Establishes RCT-level efficacy of cannabidiol across three DEE syndromes.
      The reported median seizure reductions of 38.9%, 41.9% and 48.6% follow
      immediately in the source but are interleaved with inline citation
      markers, so the quote stops before them.
- name: Fenfluramine
  description: >-
    Serotonergic agent approved as add-on therapy for Dravet syndrome and
    subsequently for Lennox-Gastaut syndrome and CDKL5 deficiency disorder.
    Requires cardiac monitoring given the valvulopathy concerns arising from its
    former use as an obesity drug.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pharmacotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15986
      label: Pharmacotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: fenfluramine
      term:
        id: CHEBI:5000
        label: fenfluramine
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Hypersynchronous Network Activity and Seizures
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
    description: >-
      Symptomatic suppression of seizure generation via serotonergic modulation.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:39237642
      reference_title: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        The higher
        dose of fenfluramine was associated with a significantly greater
        likelihood of achieving a >50% (68% versus 12% placebo) and a >75%
        reduction (50% versus 2% placebo) in convulsive seizure frequency
      explanation: >-
        RCT evidence of dose-dependent convulsive-seizure reduction, targeting
        the seizure node.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39237642
    reference_title: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The higher
      dose of fenfluramine was associated with a significantly greater
      likelihood of achieving a >50% (68% versus 12% placebo) and a >75%
      reduction (50% versus 2% placebo) in convulsive seizure frequency
    explanation: >-
      Documents dose-dependent RCT efficacy of fenfluramine as add-on therapy in
      Dravet syndrome, with the effect sizes quoted.
- name: Stiripentol
  description: >-
    Approved as adjunctive therapy for Dravet syndrome in combination with
    clobazam, where a randomised controlled trial demonstrated clear efficacy.
    CHEBI has no stiripentol term, so the agent is bound to NCIT following the
    documented NCIT-fallback convention for drugs lacking a CHEBI entry.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pharmacotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15986
      label: Pharmacotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: stiripentol
      term:
        id: NCIT:C152433
        label: Stiripentol
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Hypersynchronous Network Activity and Seizures
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
    description: >-
      Symptomatic suppression of seizure generation, used in combination with
      clobazam.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:39237642
      reference_title: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        In Dravet syndrome, a RCT of stiripentol demonstrated clear efficacy
      explanation: >-
        RCT evidence that stiripentol acts on the seizure arm in the archetypal
        genetic DEE.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39237642
    reference_title: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      In Dravet syndrome, a RCT of stiripentol demonstrated clear efficacy
    explanation: >-
      Establishes RCT-level efficacy of stiripentol in the archetypal genetic
      DEE.
- name: Multidisciplinary Developmental Supportive Care
  description: >-
    Physical, occupational, and speech therapy along with early
    intervention services to support developmental outcomes independent
    of seizure control.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: supportive care
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15747
      label: Supportive Care
  therapeutic_modality: BEHAVIORAL
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Developmental Encephalopathy Component
    treatment_effect: MODULATES
    description: >-
      Developmental and rehabilitative support addresses the developmental arm
      of the mechanism, which persists independently of seizure control and is
      therefore not reachable by antiseizure therapy.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:39237642
      reference_title: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        Problems
        change with age and patients require substantial support throughout
        life, placing a high psychosocial burden on parents, carers and the
        community.
      explanation: >-
        Supports lifelong developmental support as the management response to
        the non-seizure arm of the disease.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39237642
    reference_title: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Problems
      change with age and patients require substantial support throughout life,
      placing a high psychosocial burden on parents, carers and the community.
    explanation: >-
      Supports lifelong multidisciplinary supportive care as a core management
      component independent of seizure control.
- name: Precision Medicine Guided by Molecular Diagnosis
  description: >-
    Identification of the specific causal gene and the functional direction of
    the variant (gain- versus loss-of-function) enables aetiology-directed
    therapy selection and is increasingly the entry point to gene-targeted
    treatments including antisense oligonucleotides and gene therapy.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Targeted Therapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C93352
      label: Targeted Therapy
  therapeutic_modality: OTHER
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Genetic Lesion in an Ion Channel or Synaptic Gene
    treatment_effect: MODULATES
    description: >-
      The only entry-level treatment addressing the upstream cause rather than
      the seizure output. Establishing the specific gene and the functional
      direction of the variant redirects therapy at the lesion itself, and is
      the gateway to gene-targeted modalities (antisense oligonucleotides, gene
      therapy) still in development.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:39237642
      reference_title: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        Identification of the underlying aetiology enables the development of
        precision medicines to improve the long-term outcome of patients with
        these devastating diseases.
      explanation: >-
        Supports the aetiology-directed link from molecular diagnosis back to
        the causal genetic lesion node.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39237642
    reference_title: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Identification of the underlying aetiology enables the development of
      precision medicines to improve the long-term outcome of patients with
      these devastating diseases.
    explanation: >-
      Supports molecular diagnosis as the enabler of precision therapy in the
      DEE group.
  - reference: PMID:35701389
    reference_title: Exome sequencing for patients with developmental and epileptic encephalopathies in clinical practice.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Finding the molecular cause led to management changes in 36% of patients
      with DEEs.
    explanation: >-
      Quantifies the clinical actionability of molecular diagnosis in a
      real-world DEE cohort.
diagnosis:
- name: Exome or Genome Sequencing
  description: >-
    Genome-wide sequencing (exome or genome, ideally as a trio to enable de novo
    confirmation) is the first-line molecular test given the extreme genetic
    heterogeneity of the group. Diagnostic yield is substantially higher for
    seizure onset under two years of age.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:35701389
    reference_title: Exome sequencing for patients with developmental and epileptic encephalopathies in clinical practice.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Of the 103 patients recruited (54 males, 49 females; aged
      2 weeks-17 years), the genetic aetiology was identified in 36 out of 103
      (35%) with management implications in 13 out of 36.
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the diagnostic yield of exome sequencing in routine clinical
      care of children with DEE.
  - reference: PMID:35701389
    reference_title: Exome sequencing for patients with developmental and epileptic encephalopathies in clinical practice.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Genetic aetiology was identified in 41% of children with seizure onset
      under 2 years, compared to 18% with older onset.
    explanation: >-
      Documents the age-of-onset dependence of diagnostic yield, informing test
      prioritisation.

  title: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.

datasets:
- accession: geo:GSE319080
  title: Excitatory cortical neurons from CDKL5 deficiency disorder patient-derived organoids show early hyperexcitability not identified in neurogenin2 induced neurons [Ampliseq]
  description: CDKL5 deficiency disorder (CDD) is a rare developmental and epileptic encephalopathy resulting from variants in cyclin-dependent kinase-like 5 (CDKL5) that lead to impaired kinase activity or loss of function. CDD is one of the most common genetic etiologies identified in epilepsy cohorts. To study how CDKL5 variants impact human neuronal activity, gene expression and morphology, CDD patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells and their isogenic controls were differentiated into excitatory neurons using either an NGN2 induction protocol or a guided cortical organoid differentiation.
  organism:
    preferred_term: human
    term:
      id: NCBITaxon:9606
      label: Homo sapiens
  sample_count: 12
  publication: PMID:40930428
  notes: Identified by GEO DataSets index search for Genetic Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy (scripts/discover_datasets.py); accession and metadata verified against NCBI E-utilities on 2026-08-01. Title, sample count, and organism are GEO's own values.
- accession: geo:GSE281622
  title: Cortical versus hippocampal network dysfunction in a human brain assembloid model of epilepsy and intellectual disability
  description: Neurodevelopmental disorders often impair multiple cognitive domains. For instance, a genetic epilepsy syndrome might cause seizures due to cortical hyperexcitability and present with memory impairments arising from hippocampal dysfunction. Create: Genetic Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy · 2026-07-31T00:45:00Z · View source

Created the umbrella entry for genetic DEE [MONDO:0100062], verified by direct OAK lookup and distinct from the ~40 gene-specific DEE entries already in the KB, which MONDO places as its children. Duplicate preflight across origin/main, PRs and issues found no existing coverage. Deep research providers: falcon [Edison] and claude_code, both run via `just research-disorder`. Reports and citations committed under research/. Both reports agreed on the core mechanism; falcon additionally cautioned against assigning an unverified umbrella identifier, and the claude_code report misidentified the umbrella MONDO as MONDO:0010246 -- the OAK-verified MONDO:0100062 was used instead. Modeled the two-component DEE mechanism from the 2017 ILAE classification: a genetic lesion in an ion-channel or synaptic gene drives excitation-inhibition imbalance, which branches into a seizure/epileptic-encephalopathy arm and an independent impaired-neurodevelopment arm. Conforms to the epilepsy_excitation_inhibition_imbalance module at the E/I-imbalance and hyperexcitability nodes. Curated 48 evidence items across pathophysiology nodes, causal edges, phenotypes, genetic, prevalence, inheritance, diagnosis and treatments. Added four causative genes -- SCN1A, KCNQ2, SCN2A, STXBP1 -- with per-gene case fractions from the Italian national survey [PMID:39613335], plus a genetic-DEE-specific prevalence figure from the same source and DEE-overall figures from the New Zealand population cohort [PMID:36581463], marked PARTIAL since they cover DEE of all etiologies. Corrected two claims during curation: the gene count was raised from "over one hundred" to "more than nine hundred" per PMID:39237642, and the inheritance section was reworked to distinguish gene-count from case-count -- more DEE genes follow autosomal recessive than dominant inheritance, while 77 percent of diagnosed cases involve autosomal dominant genes. Validation: `just validate` passes for schema, terms and references. All 48 snippets were independently verified as exact whitespace-normalized substrings of their cached PubMed abstracts via a standalone check, an earlier note in this record claimed `just validate-references` was a no-op false-green because it reports "Total checks: 0"; that was wrong. A deliberate-corruption test showed it correctly rejects fabricated snippets against both abstract-only and full-text caches -- "Total checks" counts issues found, not snippets examined. Compliance 98.2 percent global / 99.1 percent weighted.
